For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

articles.title: Cambridge University professor resigns after major plagiarism accusations prompt investigation
articles.excerpt: Nikki Neily of Defending Education warns against controversial teacher training programs in over 20 states that push radical theories, undermining parental authority. She argues these programs use stu...
articles.body_text:
Nikki Neily of Defending Education warns against controversial teacher training programs in over 20 states that push radical theories, undermining parental authority. She argues these programs use students as child soldiers for social change.

University of Cambridge sociology professor Jason Arday resigned Wednesday after the university announced an investigation into his academic qualifications and honorary appointments amid plagiarism accusations, with one accuser telling Fox that Arday had been hired to be the "face of DEI."

Accusations against Arday surfaced last month from former Cambridge philosophy researcher Nathan Cofnas, who published a Substack article alleging that Arday was a known "plagiarist and fabulist" for more than a year, and much of his personal biography was questionable.

"I am disappointed that Jason Arday resigned. He was hired by Cambridge to be the face of DEI, and he was doing a great job," Cofnas told Fox News Digital.

Cofnas first expressed doubt about Arday's background after the educator said he had been nonverbal until age eleven and practically illiterate until 18 while still being able to get a Ph.D in 2015 and become the youngest Black professor at Cambridge University in 2023.

NEW YORK MAGAZINE COLUMNIST ACCUSED OF PLAGIARISM BY FELLOW REPORTERS, TRIGGERS INTERNAL REVIEW

Cambridge University sociology professor Jason Arday was accused of plagiarizing several papers, including his 2015 dissertation. (iStock)

Using the plagiarism-detection program, Copyleaks, Cofnas said he found several examples of Arday directly lifting materials from a 2009 dissertation without proper citation and sometimes even retaining copy-editing mistakes. Other earlier papers written by Arday were also issued corrections to add more citations, which Cofnas characterized as an admission of plagiarism.

From his research, Cofnas accused the university of hiring Arday to push diversity politics and has since been attempting to cover up plagiarism accusations to protect him from scrutiny.

"When you take away the work that is plagiarized or not otherwise written by Arday, there is essentially nothing resembling real scholarship," Cofnas wrote. "There is no indication that Arday is familiar with even elementary statistics. His research involves reporting his own experiences of alleged racism or having conversations with people and providing subjective commentary."

Arday's appointment in 2023 received massive media attention, with much of it celebrating it as a landmark moment.

Other media outlets and academics began reporting on the accusations, however, such as the Telegraph, the Guardian and the Times of London. Cambridge University initially stood by Arday in a statement on Sunday, saying Arday had already been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University and other journals for plagiarism. However, by Wednesday, Cambridge announced it was reversing course.

HARVARD CHIEF DEI OFFICER ACCUSED OF 40 COUNTS OF PLAGIARISM, INCLUDING LIFTING FROM HER OWN HUSBAND: REPORT

University of Cambridge announced an investigation into Jason Arday on Wednesday. (Igor Golovniov/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Image)

"The University of Cambridge has begun an investigation following new information about Professor Arday’s academic qualifications and honorary appointments. In order to ensure a fair process, we will not comment further until this has concluded," the statement read.

Shortly after the statement was released, Arday released his own statement through the Good Law Project announcing that he was resigning with "immediate effect," noting "public scrutiny" as a factor.

"Sadly, the years since my appointment have also been marked by an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack. While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement. The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love," Arday wrote.

HARVARD ATTEMPTING TO ‘REDEFINE’ PLAGIARISM TO PROTECT EMBATTLED PRESIDENT CLAUDINE GAY, ALLEGED VICTIM SAYS

He continued, "I have tried to continue because I believe deeply in the values of higher education, in rigorous scholarship, and in the transformative power of universities. I have tried because of my students, my colleagues and the countless people who have written to tell me that my journey gave them hope. But there comes a point when the personal cost becomes too great."

Arday announced on Wednesday that he would be leaving the university effective immediately. (Tu xa Ha Noi via Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to Cambridge University and Arday for comment.

Cofnas added to Fox News Digital, "However, given that he is gone, a number of people have suggested that his professorship should be given to me. If the Cambridge administration could arrange this, it would go a long way toward restoring trust in higher education."

Cofnas was ousted from Cambridge in 2024 amid criticism of his writing that Blacks would almost completely "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment" in a world of full meritocracy.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Vehicle narrowly avoids slamming into driver on side of Ohio highway, dramatic video shows
articles.excerpt:
A driver who exited his vehicle on Ohio's Highway 270 avoided death by jumping out of the way of a car that smashed into his SUV on the side of the highway. Credit: Ohio Department of Transportation.
...
articles.body_text:
A driver who exited his vehicle on Ohio's Highway 270 avoided death by jumping out of the way of a car that smashed into his SUV on the side of the highway. Credit: Ohio Department of Transportation.

A vehicle narrowly avoided slamming into a driver on the side of an Ohio highway Monday, video released by the state Department of Transportation shows.

The motorist was standing along Columbus' I-670 adjacent to his vehicle, which was parallel to the road after seemingly striking the highway divider.

Video then shows a sedan careening toward the driver and his vehicle. The man, noticing the oncoming vehicle, hoists himself onto the highway median at the last second. The oncoming vehicle then smashes into his SUV, the footage shows.

WATCH: DASHCAM CAPTURES THE SPLIT SECOND A ROUTINE TENNESSEE TRAFFIC STOP GOES SIDEWAYS

Emergency crews assist after a car crash on the side of Ohio's Highway 670. (Ohio Department of Transportation)

According to a 911 call obtained by local news outlet ABC6, the SUV had a passenger in it at the time of impact.

The passenger told 911 operators that their vehicle had lost a tire and hit the highway divider before the crash.

"It’s off to the side but we are right in the turnstile, and it's really worrying me because we’re going to get hit," the passenger told operators, according to ABC6.

Vehicles drive on Interstate 670 near the Cleveland Avenue bridge on Tuesday, April 7, 2026, in Columbus, Ohio. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Fox News Digital contacted the Ohio Department of Transportation for updates on the conditions of the passengers involved.

TRUMP TAPS VETERANS TO FIX ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKING PROBLEM PLAGUING US ROADWAYS

A department spokesman highlighted the incident as a safety lesson, noting that the lane the impacted vehicle was in was closed and should not have had any other cars driving in it.

Ohio Department of Transportation Alexandria Outpost on Aug. 1, 2026, in Alexandria, Ohio. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"There will be a green arrow over it if it's opened, a red X if it is closed. In this case, it was an emergency shoulder, so the person who crashed was stopped on the shoulder of the highway. They were doing the right thing. There should be nobody driving in that lane," Ohio Department of Transportation press secretary Matt Bruning told reporters.

The emergency lane, Bruning explained to Fox News Digital, was a "SmartLane," a highway feature in Ohio that allows the state to convert the wide shoulder into a temporary travel lane as needed. The SmartLane was closed at the time of the crash.

"Don't drive in a closed lane. If you are going to drive on the highway, allow that extra space between you and the vehicle in front of you so you have time to react and space to react if something might happen," Bruning concluded.

articles.title: Seven killed after teen shooter opens fire at home and school in Thailand
articles.excerpt:

At least seven people have been killed and 23 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand's c...
articles.body_text:
Police have been combing over the school for evidence

At least seven people have been killed and 23 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand's capital Bangkok.

The gunman - a student at the Debsirin School in Nonthaburi - killed his grandparents and five teachers before taking his own life, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters. The attacker still had "more than 30 bullets left" when he turned the gun on himself, Anutin added.

Nine of the injured people remain in a critical condition, authorities say.

The shooting - the second at a school in Thailand this year - has renewed pressure on the government for greater action on gun control.

Police were deployed to the scene during the active shooting, which began just after 10:00 local time (03:00 GMT).

National police chief police general Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the gunman's shots were quite accurate, with several hitting vital spots on the body.

The prime minister said the attack was "well prepared" with "clear steps and clear goals".

The attacker has not been publicly named, and police haven't disclosed a motive - though the prime minister said the boy may have been stressed about his studies.

Investigations are continuing, with officers seen carrying away computer equipment and boxes from the home the shooter shared with his grandparents, who he shot dead before the school rampage.

I was standing in front of my teacher when she was shot, Thai pupil says

The Debsirin School, founded in Bangkok in 1885, is one of Thailand's top secondary schools with branches across the country. It counts many prominent Thai figures as its alumni, from diplomats and athletes to several prime ministers.

A female seventh grader, still in school uniform, told the BBC she was standing in front of her teacher when the woman was shot.

"She was talking to me when [the gunman] showed up and shot her," she said.

"I couldn't see anything but a [cloud] of dust."

Still in her uniform, with her mother by her side, she explained how the shooter stalked from room to room.

"I had to climb over the school fence to escape with other friends."

Her mother says the girl thought she might die. "[She said] 'I thought I'd never see you again'."

Another student told Reuters news agency that he had thought the sound of gunshots were firecrackers going off.

"There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."

Students and school staff were seen fleeing from the scene, and those waiting outside the Debsirin School looked visibly distraught.

Authorities warned people to stay away from the area and for those trapped in the building to hide and wait for rescuers.

Students shelter in classroom as gunshots heard

In a post on social media, the school later shared a call for blood donations.

Other schools in the vicinity suspended classes so students could return home early.

PM Anutin expressed condolences for the victims of the school shooting. He said the tragedy "shouldn't have happened", adding "this is why the government do not allow [citizens] to possess firearms".

"I don't just feel sorry for the victims but I feel sorry that this happened. How can this happen in our country," he said.

Thailand has strict gun laws, which punishes the illegal possession of arms with up to 10 years in jail. Enforcement of these laws has been an issue - though police have made no suggestion the weapon used in this case, owned by the shooter's grandfather, was illegally obtained.

The country has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in South East Asia. It is estimated that about 40% of these guns are illegal.

Friday's shooting immediately triggered calls from politicians for a review of the current gun laws.

Prime Minister Anutin responded by pledging to introduce a new firearms control law.

Under the proposed new legislation, there will be restrictions on members of the public carrying such weapons.

"The new law will only allow government officials on duty to carry guns," Anutin said.

He did not provide any specifics for the proposed legislation, including whether it would tighten gun ownership requirements.

articles.title: Sri Lanka prisoners riot leaving 3 dead, 23 injured in chaos
articles.excerpt:
Police and riot squads have been deployed after three inmates were killed and nearly two dozen others were injured in separate prison riots across Sri Lanka.

Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala ...
articles.body_text:
Police and riot squads have been deployed after three inmates were killed and nearly two dozen others were injured in separate prison riots across Sri Lanka.

Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala told parliament on Friday that one prisoner was killed when 40 inmates broke out of their cells at the New Magazine Prison in the capital, Colombo, late on Thursday.

Two more prisoners were killed on Friday morning during a second riot at Kuruwita prison, about 80km (50 miles) from the capital, he said.

Between the two incidents, 23 inmates were injured and admitted to hospitals, Wijepala said, adding that police and special forces ‌brought both riots under control.

Additionally, police told the Reuters news agency that officers fired tear gas at protesting inmates at an open prison in the coastal town of Negombo, about 40km (25 miles) from Colombo, to bring the situation there under control on Friday.

Riot police at all three prisons worked to return prisoners who had climbed onto rooftops or moved into open areas back to their wards, the minister said.

Wijepala told parliament the violence was related to narcotics dealers and rival criminal gangs.

He said the government is trying to find out if the riots were coordinated.

“When you take all ⁠these incidents together, it appears that there is planning behind these and an attempt at sabotage. But we can only say ⁠anything further after a comprehensive investigation,” Wijepala said.

The prison disturbances happened a month after 10 ⁠prison officials and 20 prisoners died in two days of fighting at a prison in Negombo.

One inmate also died and several others ‌were injured in a riot last weekend at a prison in Mahara, about 14km (8.6 miles) from Colombo.

Overcrowding in Sri Lanka’s prisons is at crisis levels.

Facilities are highly congested, with more than 39,000 inmates crowded into a system with a total capacity of just 10,000, according to a recent speech in parliament by Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara.

“The number of prisoners in Sri Lanka today is four times the capacity,” said Senaka Perera, president of the Committee for Rights of Prisoners. “In fact, they have been patient for so long.”

A large number of inmates are suspects awaiting trial for alleged narcotics-related offences. Recent laws tightening bail conditions have resulted in prison overcrowding, Perera said.

Sri Lanka is planning to amend its constitution ‌to extend superior court judges’ tenure by two years, as part of efforts to clear a backlog of more than one million court cases and reduce prisoner numbers.

articles.title: ICE will not reveal body-camera footage unless in agency’s ‘best interests’
articles.excerpt:
Much-delayed devices to be deployed by end of month after immigration agents involved in deaths or serious injuries

Officers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) will be equipped with much-d...
articles.body_text:
Much-delayed devices to be deployed by end of month after immigration agents involved in deaths or serious injuries

Officers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) will be equipped with much-delayed body cameras by the end of next month, it was reported on Friday. But experts have questioned the transparency of a policy that allows the ICE director to restrict the public release of footage unless “it is in the best interests of the agency”.

Pressure has mounted on the Trump administration to provide body cameras after people caught up in encounters with federal immigration personnel suffered death or serious injuries.

Two men were shot and killed by ICE agents, in Texas and Maine, last month in circumstances similar to the death of another man during a traffic stop in Illinois last September. None of the officers involved was wearing a camera.

Tom Homan, Trump’s so-called border czar, said last month that ICE officers would be required to have at least one body camera recording during future vehicle stops. Policy for body-worn cameras was first established in a February 2025 ICE directive, but funding for their provision was held up by this year’s partial government shutdown, Homan said.

The intention of using such cameras, according to David Venturella, the ICE acting director, is to increase transparency and accountability.

One analyst, however, told the Associated Press that an accompanying “selective release” policy of footage meant taxpayers who put up more than $30m for the cameras may still be kept in the dark about some high-profile confrontations, at least in their immediate aftermath.

Christopher Schneider, a sociology professor at Canada’s Brandon University, and co-author of Police Body-Worn Cameras: Media and the New Discourse of Police Reform, said the ICE director would have discretion to release recordings that reflect well on the agency’s image while working to keep others secret.

“In some ways, ICE is saying the quiet part out loud,” he said. “Body-worn cameras are being used as contemporary image-work tools to present the police to the public in the most favorable way possible.”

The policy says ICE will promptly release video of shootings and other encounters in which its agents cause death or serious injury only after determining “it is in the best interests of the agency” to do so.

It requires officers to activate cameras during routine enforcement activities, including while making arrests, executing search warrants and responding to emergencies.

After shootings or other serious confrontations, a committee that includes top ICE officials and lawyers will review footage and recommend whether to release it promptly, according to the February 2025 policy.

If the ICE director finds that “specific and compelling circumstances” justify withholding the video, they have the authority to block or indefinitely delay the release, the policy says.

The Trump administration slow-walked a pilot program last year to provide cameras to ICE personnel, it was reported in January, and moved to cut funding.

Civilian cellphone footage of the deaths of protesters Renee Good and Alex Pretti at the hands of federal immigration officers in separate January incidents in Minneapolis allowed their families and supporters to challenge authorities’ accounts of the encounters.

Homan, in a TV appearance on Fox & Friends last month, said he welcomed the imminent rollout of the cameras.

“They exonerate more law enforcement than they convict, and I want officers to wear body cameras because I want the American people to see what the ⁠officers saw when they took that action,” he said.

The Associated Press contributed to this report

articles.title: Ex-Obama, Biden diplomat blasts former boss’ border failures: 'They woke up too late'
articles.excerpt: Former Interior Secretary and ex-Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar said the Biden White House made Mexico and the Americas a low priority, lacked urgency, planning and a comms strategy. He said Trump m...
articles.body_text:
Former Interior Secretary and ex-Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar said the Biden White House made Mexico and the Americas a low priority, lacked urgency, planning and a comms strategy. He said Trump made the border

Former Cabinet secretary and U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar says the Biden administration "woke up too late" to address the border crisis, arguing its failure to prioritize Mexico and effectively communicate its strategy helped hand President Donald Trump one of his strongest political issues.

Salazar, whose family has lived in the southwest since it was part of Mexico, laid out in his new book "Borderlands" how America’s foreign policy is too often on an "east-west paradigm" looking to Asia and Europe and neglecting Mexico and the Americas. He also argued that same mindset plagued the Biden administration, leaving it overly focused on Europe and Asia while neglecting Mexico and the Western Hemisphere.

"From day one, there should have been a great sense of urgency in addressing the crisis of a broken border and the migration crisis that we are seeing," Salazar said, arguing the Biden White House lacked both a comprehensive strategy and a coherent communications operation, creating what he described as a communications vacuum that Republicans filled.

BOMBSHELL MEMO SHOWS BIDEN PLANNED TO LEAVE TRUMP WITH EVEN MORE MASSIVE IMMIGRATION CRISIS

President Biden, left; Ken Salazar, right. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"I think that's what trapped the administration into this sense that they woke up too late by the time they did the right things to get control of the border," he said.

In the book, he recounts nearly resigning from his ambassadorship during a visit to Mexico with Biden and several inner-circle officials after being left out of an important meeting where he wanted to make the case for appointing a border-and-migration czar.

After one meeting at the Palacio Nacional in Mexico City, Salazar wrote that he decided to present his plan the next day but found out that he and former Sen. Christopher Dodd, D-Conn., weren’t going to be in the key meeting the next day.

Ultimately, he was able to meet privately with Biden at the last minute, where he expressed his concerns:

"We need someone in the White House to oversee the border, migration, Mexico, and the Americas. No one is in charge now. We need a border and migration czar," he said, reminding Biden that adviser Jeffrey Zients served as a "czar" for the COVID-19 response.

"[We need] someone focused exclusively on this crisis, with the authority to coordinate and direct action across agencies in Washington and communicate the message with one voice on these issues. With all due respect, Mr. President, if we are to succeed, it is urgent that we have someone like this in charge."

Salazar wrote that even after Biden's June 2024 executive order sharply reduced crossings, the administration failed to communicate the policy's success before Biden exited the race..

He said that gave President Donald Trump an opportunity to campaign on the "low-hanging fruit" of the border crisis.

TANVI RATNA: LATIN AMERICA'S RIGHT TURN IS REDRAWING THE UNITED STATES' BACKYARD

A split screen of former U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ken Salazar and President Joe Biden. Salazar criticized Biden and his administrations handling of the border crisis and revealed he almost ran for president in 2024. (Matt Kelley/AP Photo)

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Biden for comment.

Both Biden and Trump, however, displayed what Salazar called "foreign policy malpractice" in terms of the Americas — something administrations have struggled with for 100 years, according to Salazar.

"That’s where everybody gets trapped," he said.

"Republicans, like Donald Trump, use it as a political advantage because that's how they win elections. And they realized that way back 20-some years ago."

"Democrats, on the other hand, have a sense that it is very important. And they do focus, but only on the border and on domestic migration issues [like] immigration reform. They don't focus at all or enough on Mexico [or] the border between Mexico and Guatemala — And that's what I believe we have to do. And that is what 'Borderlands' proposes that we do," he said, referring to his book.

HARRIS CALLS FOR ICE PROBE AFTER MAINE SHOOTING AMID RENEWED 'BORDER CZAR' CRITICISM

WASHINGTON - FEBRUARY 12: U.S. Interior Secretary Ken Salazar speaks during an Abraham Lincoln birthday celebration event at the Lincoln Memorial February 12, 2009 in Washington, DC. Thursday marked the 200th birthday of the 16th President of the United States Abraham Lincoln. (Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)

TRUMP BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN WANTS POPE LEO XIV TO RIDE ALONG WITH ICE AGENTS: 'THEY DON'T UNDERSTAND'

Instead of demonizing migrants or focusing only on social aspects of the crisis, Salazar said his "Borderlands Platform" is a new vision that is grounded in realizing economic and national security prosperity for all three North American countries.

Salazar's proposed "Borderlands Platform" calls for a "New American Alliance" among the United States, Mexico and Canada, including deeper security cooperation, expanded labor mobility and renewed investment in North American trade. He argued immigration policy should be treated as both a national security and economic issue rather than solely a domestic political fight — and wrote supportively about renewing Trump’s USMCA, which had supplanted Bill Clinton’s NAFTA.

Salazar said Trump is correct that the border is "broken," but said he disagreed with Trump's approach, calling it divisive and pointing to ICE-involved shootings.

"It's not the American way where people have rights, where you have a sense of security, understand the importance of our security within our own country and the importance for supporting law enforcement."

Salazar pointed to his tenure as Colorado attorney general, where he led "thousands of cops," as evidence of his longstanding support for law enforcement.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

"What is being neglected here is the bigger picture. And that's this foreign policy paradigm that is so required for the United States and Mexico and the Americas. And I don't see this administration moving in that direction to create the kind of legal frameworks that are essential that will give us our national security and ensure that we have a border that works and ensure we have an immigration system that is reformed and does the right thing," he said.

Salazar confirmed he has met with several Democrats viewed as potential 2028 presidential contenders, strongly advising them to make border and migration policy a top issue.

"Not that I have a lot of sway, but at least I will do everything I can to make sure that this is at the heart of every Democrat running for president," he said, noting that Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., was one lawmaker who met with him and endorsed his "Borderlands" book.

Asked if he would entertain Republican invitations, Salazar said if Trump reached out he would meet with him, but underlined that he would not become "political fodder for anybody."

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

"I do think that the Trump administration has an opportunity here because they, at the end of the day, recognize that the big questions of our time are affordability for the American people. The cost of strawberries, blueberries, and avocados, food, fuel, all those things are very much impacted by what's happening with tariffs and the uncertainty with Mexico right now," he said.

"I spent a lot of time on our ranch, I pumped the diesel into our [machinery], and I can tell you that across rural America, people are hurting because of what's happening with trade and we are losing a lot of our advantage here. Agriculture is in for a very hard time in the years ahead."

He said he hopes Trump would consider a "Borderlands"-type plan for a "new era" in Intracontinental relations.

"I don’t think that’s going to happen, but I certainly would give him that advice."

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

articles.title: Pentagon plots new nuclear options for Trump as America’s biggest adversaries raise stakes: report
articles.excerpt: US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker discusses escalating U.S.-Iran tensions amid reports of Chinese missile transfers to Tehran. He also addresses Russia's missile attack on Kyiv after Zelenskyy's ...
articles.body_text:
US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker discusses escalating U.S.-Iran tensions amid reports of Chinese missile transfers to Tehran. He also addresses Russia's missile attack on Kyiv after Zelenskyy's warning and Ukraine's urgent need for air defense.

The Pentagon is drafting a new nuclear strategy aimed at giving President Donald Trump more options for using shorter-range nuclear weapons in a potential regional conflict with China or Russia, according to a report.

The classified effort, led by Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby, would put greater emphasis on tactical nuclear weapons — systems intended for use against military targets in a regional conflict — rather than relying primarily on long-range strategic forces, NBC News reported, citing five people familiar with the plans.

The strategy is designed for scenarios in which China or Russia attacks a U.S. ally and Washington must determine how to respond without immediately escalating to a large-scale strategic nuclear exchange, according to the report.

TRUMP HEADS TO BEIJING FOR HIGH-STAKES XI TALKS AS TAIWAN TENSIONS, TRADE DISPUTES TEST US STRENGTH

FILE - This photo taken from video provided by the Russian Defense Ministry Press Service on Feb. 19, 2022, shows a Yars intercontinental ballistic missile being launched from an air field during military drills in Russia. The Russian Defense Ministry said that the military will hold drills involving tactical nuclear weapons – the first time such exercise was publicly announced by Moscow. (Russian Defense Ministry Press Service via AP, File) (Russian Defense Ministry Press Service via AP)

"Our view is that we need credible nuclear options," a senior War Department official told NBC. The official said the strategy would "expand the President’s option space by providing him with realistic and credible options and therefore strengthen deterrence."

The reported shift comes as the United States confronts two nuclear-armed adversaries with increasingly capable arsenals.

Russia retains a large stockpile of theater nuclear weapons and has repeatedly invoked its nuclear capabilities during the war in Ukraine. China, meanwhile, is rapidly expanding and modernizing its nuclear forces, creating what U.S. military officials increasingly describe as a two-peer nuclear challenge.

Tactical, or non-strategic, nuclear weapons are generally designed for theater or regional use rather than long-range strategic missions. They often have shorter-range delivery systems and may be intended for military targets.

But the label does not mean they are limited in consequence: a nuclear detonation could kill large numbers of people, spread radioactive fallout and trigger nuclear retaliation.

US FALLS BEHIND IN HYPERSONIC RACE AS CHINA, RUSSIA GAIN EDGE

China may be conducting low-yield nuclear tests, a State Department official says. (Tingshu Wang/File Photo/Reuters)

The War Department has not publicly announced a change in nuclear employment policy or a new tactical nuclear weapons program. Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon for comment.

The review also comes six months after New START, the last treaty limiting U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals, expired without a replacement, leaving Washington and Moscow without binding limits or inspections for the first time in decades.

The treaty did not cover tactical nuclear weapons, an area in which Russia holds a substantial numerical advantage. U.S. Strategic Command estimated this year that Moscow possesses up to 2,000 theater nuclear warheads.

An unarmed LGM-30G Minuteman III sits inside the silo of U-01 at F.E. Warren Air Force Base, Wyoming, July 9, 2025. (Staff Sgt. Michael A. Richmond/U.S. Air Force)

Russia has long relied on its non-strategic nuclear arsenal in part to offset NATO’s conventional military strength. China’s growing arsenal is adding a separate challenge for Pentagon planners preparing for the possibility of confronting two nuclear-armed competitors.

Supporters of the Pentagon’s reported shift argue that giving Trump more credible limited-response options could strengthen deterrence by convincing an adversary that Washington has ways to respond short of an all-out strategic exchange.

Critics argue that putting greater emphasis on weapons intended for regional use could lower the threshold for nuclear employment and increase the risk that a limited conflict spirals into a broader nuclear war.

articles.title: The “Protect College Sports Act" has a fatal flaw: It doesn’t protect women | Riley Gaines
articles.excerpt:
Leigh Ross-Dakich explains that the women who helped build up girls sports are now having to be quiet about the trans athlete issue.

I’ve stood on the starting block knowing the race was already rigg...
articles.body_text:
Leigh Ross-Dakich explains that the women who helped build up girls sports are now having to be quiet about the trans athlete issue.

I’ve stood on the starting block knowing the race was already rigged. I’ve touched the wall at the same time as a male competitor and been told to smile for the cameras. So when Congress names a bill the "Protect College Sports Act," I pay attention.

The Protect College Sports Act sounds great. Who wouldn’t want to protect college sports? But buried in dozens of pages about athlete compensation and coaching transitions is language that threatens existing state laws, including laws that protect fairness in women's sports.

Riley Gaines and Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham pose for a photo following Sunday's game at Target Center against the Minnesota Lynx. (Riley Gaines/XX-XY Athletics)

As someone who knows firsthand the devastation of watching the trophy you spent years training to win be handed to a physically dominant male competitor, and then experiencing the shock of seeing that same male expose himself to other girls as he undresses in the locker room, I have a personal stake in making sure no other young woman goes through that. I’ve spent years traveling across the country with other athletes, sharing our experiences with state lawmakers and Congress, urging them to pass common-sense laws that keep men off the girls’ playing field and out of girls’ locker rooms.

REPUBLICAN SENATORS FILE AMENDMENT TO STOP COLLEGE SPORTS BILL FROM OVERRIDING STATE WOMEN'S SPORTS LAWS

A total of 27 states now have these laws. President Trump signed an executive order recognizing that men are men, women are women, and guys don't belong in girls' sports. Because of this work, countless young women have been guaranteed that males will not invade their sports.

University of Pennsylvania swimmer Lia Thomas and Kentucky swimmer Riley Gaines react after finishing tied for fifth in the 200 freestyle finals at the NCAA Swimming and Diving Championships on March 18th, 2022 at the McAuley Aquatic Center in Atlanta, Georgia. (Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

But the Protect College Sports Act puts all of those laws and all of the work to pass them at risk. The same trans-activists who screamed at me in legislatures and harassed me at colleges could misuse the Protect College Sports Act to challenge every single state law defending women’s athletic competition…all 27 of them. That’s not protecting college sports for young women. It’s protecting the NCAA.

One of the critical flaws with the bill is that it limits the ability of states to enact or enforce sports eligibility rules. It's easy to envision a male who insists he belongs on a women's team misusing the bill to argue that a state women's sports law (which says males are not eligible to be on women's teams) is no longer valid.

The bill has another critical problem: It trusts the national athletic associations—namely the NCAA—to enforce state women’s sports laws.

TRUMP URGES CONGRESS TO PASS PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE RECESS: 'WE HAVE TO GET THAT DONE'

Let’s be honest about who we’d be trusting to get this right. The NCAA has never been a friend to women’s sports. It sure wasn't a friend to me or my teammates and competitors as we watched William (Lia) Thomas stand on that podium at the NCAA Swimming Championships. The NCAA opposed state-level protections early on and only changed course after massive public outcry forced its hand.

President Donald Trump joined by women athletes signs the "No Men in Women’s Sports" executive order in the East Room at the White House on February 5, 2025 in Washington, DC. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

And don’t forget how the Democrats still don’t know how to define the word "woman". Thank God President Trump does, but we have no reason to believe the next Democrat President won’t undo all of President Trump’s executive orders that have yet to be codified by Congress just as quickly as he signed them.

The bill’s supporters will tell you I’m reading it wrong. They say limitations on state laws governing eligibility should be read narrowly—that it only blocks a few specific eligibility rules, not state laws protecting women’s sports. But here’s my question: if that’s what they meant, why didn’t they just write it that way? They could fix this with a simple amendment. The fact that they haven’t tells you everything you need to know. The Democrats see the Protect College Sports Act as a Trojan Horse to appease the trans rights activists.

We spent four years under the Biden Administration as it pushed radical gender ideology every chance it got and punished the people who spoke against it. All that time, deserving young women were losing their spots on the team or their places atop the podium. Young girls were horrified walking into their locker rooms to find a male gawking at them as they undressed.

AB Hernandez stands on the first-place podium alongside a female opponent at the 2026 California track and field state championships. It was a flashpoint in the history of girls' sports. (Fox News Digital)

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Let's not re-live that nightmare. Why pass a bill that would put any young girl at risk of going through that same heartache and trauma? As a mom to a baby girl, I say no.

I’m not asking for anything radical. I’m asking for what girls in this country were promised 50 years ago: a fair shot.

No bill should pass that leaves women’s sports laws or our hard-fought Title IX protections open to being gutted. Women’s sports are not a bargaining chip.

Riley Gaines is a 12-time NCAA All-American who competed for the University of Kentucky NCAA swim team before retiring from competition and focusing on political activism. Riley is host of "The Riley Gaines Show" podcast. Watch "The Riley Gaines Show" on YouTube, or listen on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and anywhere you get your podcasts. New episodes drop Wednesdays and Fridays.

articles.title: Russia-linked accounts spread far-right narrative online during Ceuta migration crisis, analysis finds
articles.excerpt:
Counter-disinformation group says social media channels connected to Pravda network helped amplify message

Accounts with links to the Russian military promoting far-right messages reached more than 5...
articles.body_text:
Counter-disinformation group says social media channels connected to Pravda network helped amplify message

Accounts with links to the Russian military promoting far-right messages reached more than 500,000 people in the early days of the Ceuta migration crisis, according to an analysis done by 411, a counter-disinformation group.

Russia-linked social media accounts frequently spread destabilising narratives in Europe, often promoting far-right talking points about immigration.

But 411 and other experts suggest the scale and coordination of the disinformation that followed the Ceuta crisis is significant. Groups spreading disinformation are more organised and powerful than they were several years ago.

“We keep seeing this across Europe and we find it very interesting. It seems like there is some type of machinery in place, or structure,” said Saman Nazari, lead researcher at Alliance4Europe, a Brussels-based nonprofit.

“Quite regularly, we are seeing this escalation happening across Europe now, with these types of crises. It is too much of a coincidence to be a bandwagoning effect.”

The barrage began on 1 August, the day after 49,000 people reportedly attempted to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco overnight. This was part of a larger, multi-day crisis during which 72,000 migrants are estimated to have made their way into the small territory in north Africa.

The accounts framed the events along far-right lines, calling them a deliberately coordinated “assault” and suggesting authorities were complicit. Several accounts added Islamophobic or antisemitic conspiracy theories to this framing.

These narratives were rapidly reproduced in seven languages and reached more than 720,000 views over the course of six hours on 1 August, according to 411’s examination of roughly 4.5m social media posts.

Other far-right accounts called for nationalists to gather in Ceuta and “patrol” businesses and homes, some of these apparently in coordination.

Reports suggest that social media played a significant role in the crisis in Ceuta, prompting people to make the crossing and stoking a response to it. Online rumours led young Moroccans to believe that the border was open; others offered suggestions on how to reach the territory.

The analysis by 411 confirmed reports that there was substantive “peer-to-peer logistics chatter” between potential migrants on social media over how to make the crossing. Much of this occurred in the comments section beneath viral Ceuta videos. This coordination among migrants appeared to be organic, coming “overwhelmingly from small, anonymous-looking individual accounts rather than any single identifiable ‘recruiter’ channel”.

A separate, rightwing backlash began on social media as the crossings continued. One origin of the propaganda barrage was Rybar, a Telegram channel with links to Russian intelligence. Rybar’s parent company has faced sanctions in Europe.

A network of “repeater” accounts then amplified and spread Rybar’s posts. These included accounts linked to the Pravda network, an operation spreading Kremlin propaganda worldwide.

Nazari suggested that disinformation efforts appeared coordinated and that investigations should be made to determine if there were closed forums or similar structures in which far-right influencers discuss how to spread talking points.

Ned Mendez, the lead researcher at 411, said that disinformation about the Ceuta crisis spread far more quickly than it did in May 2021, during a similar incident in which 8,000 migrants crossed the same border from Morocco into Spain.

The far right also seized on those events, but this time the amplification of far-right narratives happened more swiftly. The far-right mobilisation calls brought nationalist groups to the main square of Ceuta within days, 411 noted. In 2021, similar calls went out but it took much longer for nationalists to mobilise.

“You could compare the process to a highly specific and organised information superhighway,” said Mendez. “If a piece of content or disinformation is placed on to that privileged superhighway, then it will receive a degree of amplification and boost that other types of content just don’t have access to. Events like this across Europe suggest that some pieces of content are being selected for the onramp, and those content pieces share similar characteristics.”

The 411 analysis said: “That machinery is the real thing to worry about, more than this particular crisis. The next time there’s a border incident anywhere on the Mediterranean, those same relay networks are already in place, ready to pick it up and run with it again.”

articles.title: Mad Dog Russo rips Pete Crow-Armstrong for 'derogatory' comments on Babe Ruth conspiracy theory
articles.excerpt: President Donald Trump compared Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani to Babe Ruth during the team's visit to Washington, D.C., where the team celebrated their World Series championship....
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump compared Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani to Babe Ruth during the team's visit to Washington, D.C., where the team celebrated their World Series championship. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

Pete Crow-Armstrong angered a major baseball purist when he brought up a wild conspiracy theory that Babe Ruth did not exist.

"I was like dude, that's awesome," the Chicago Cubs star and MVP favorite said recently about hearing the theory. "We always talk about how the game is evolving, and people may as well have been under handing the ball to that guy, and he's still regarded as one of the best players ever. You might as well dive further into it and be like, well maybe he just never existed."

That quote got the attention of longtime talking head and former MLB Network host Chris "Mad Dog" Russo, who said his "derogatory" comments on Ruth "drove me nuts."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Pete Crow-Armstrong recently mentioned a conspiracy theory that Babe Ruth was not real. (Getty Images)

"Hey Pete, you’re talking to me now about Ruth! Nobody hit home runs like Babe Ruth. Say what you want about [Shohei] Ohtani, we understand that he’s a unicorn. Babe Ruth is so good it’s mind boggling," Russo began on "First Take" this week. "Did you know, Peter Crow-Armstrong, that Babe Ruth hit 27 home runs over 500 feet? [Barry] Bonds? Never. Not one… Ruth owned baseball, nobody hit home runs like Ruth! He out-homered leagues!

"To sit there and say they were pitching underhand, well why didn’t anybody else hit the home runs hitting underhand? Outside of Gehrig, nobody hit home runs! It drives me crazy, especially in baseball, it drives me crazy when I hear today’s athletes and media guys who are 30 years old, who disparage the old-time guys."

Pete Crow-Armstrong #4 of the Chicago Cubs reacts to hitting a two-run home run in the third inning of a game between the Athletics and the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on June 03, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Griffin Quinn/Getty Images) (Griffin Quinn/Getty Images)

WOMAN SUES YANKEES FOR $10 MILLION, CLAIMING ERRANT BAT INTO STANDS CAUSED SEVERE INJURIES

"It drives me crazy when people think the baseball player in 1927 is not nearly as good as the baseball player today. Are you crazy?" Russo continued. "He would have been a Hall of Famer as a pitcher, forget as a hitter. There’s only one Babe Ruth. He hit anywhere, any place, any time. He’s that good. And when you start to knock Ruth…pay attention, do your homework. That was a disgrace what he said this week."

Ruth, assuming he existed, became Major League Baseball's all-time leader in home runs on July 18, 1921, with his 139th home run - he hit 575 more to retire with 714, a record that stood until Hank Aaron surpassed him in 1974.

In 1920, Babe Ruth's 54 home runs were more than the totals of seven of the eight MLB teams in existence at the time. He did the same in his 60-homer season in 1927.

Babe Ruth during the Yankees' season opener at Yankee Stadium. (Getty Images)

Ruth is the all-time leader in slugging percentage (.690) and OPS (1.164), becoming one of the game's greatest hitters after posting Hall of Fame numbers on the mound. He posted a 2.19 ERA when he was a full-time pitcher with the Boston Red Sox but pitched only 31 innings with the New York Yankees.

Lawyers for Andrew and Tristan Tate urged a ⁠US judge on Friday ⁠to release the ​broth...
articles.body_text:
Andrew and Tristan Tate remain in jail as they fight extradition to UK to face charges of rape, assault and more

Lawyers for Andrew and Tristan Tate urged a ⁠US judge on Friday ⁠to release the ​brothers from a Miami jail as they fight the British government’s efforts to extradite them to face charges of rape, assault and facilitating trafficking for ⁠sexual exploitation.

In a filing in Miami federal court, the Tate brothers’ lawyers said their “extraordinary public visibility” would make it impractical for them to try to flee, meaning there was ⁠no need to keep them behind bars until the extradition proceedings end.

“It would be extraordinarily difficult for Andrew or ​Tristan to travel undetected or avoid attention,” their ‌lawyers wrote.

They urged US magistrate ‌judge Lauren Louis to release them on bail on condition that they surrender their passports and submit to ‌location monitoring.

Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, were arrested in Miami on 18 July. Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said on 19 July it had brought new charges against the two relating to alleged offenses involving four alleged victims between July 2010 and August 2017.

The Tate brothers, both former kickboxers who are widely known as social media influencers and have dual US and British citizenship, have denied any wrongdoing.

Their arrests marked a new ‌chapter in the widening legal troubles for the brothers, who have built a large online following promoting their views on masculinity and wealth. Andrew Tate has previously described himself ​as a misogynist.

Prosecutors with the Miami US attorney’s office are due to respond to the Tates’ bid for release on bail by 10 August, and Louis has scheduled a court hearing over their possible release for 13 August.

Prosecutors have previously said Louis should keep the brothers detained because there was a risk they could flee and because ⁠they posed dangers to the community.

The legal process for determining whether the ​Tate brothers may be extradited could take ​months. Britain has until 16 September to ​submit its full extradition request to the state department, US court records show.

Andrew and Tristan Tate ‌had previously faced rape ​and human-trafficking charges ​in Britain related to three alleged victims, the CPS said. A British judge issued a warrant for their arrests in January 2024. They have not appeared in a British court to enter a plea to those charges. Britain is seeking to extradite the brothers to face both sets of charges.

articles.title: Nancy Guthrie investigators see uptick in tips after ransom notes release: Sheriff

articles.body_text:
Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos releases ransom notes sent to Savannah Guthrie after her mother, Nancy Guthrie, disappeared. Newly released surveillance footage also shows a masked suspect outside the family's Arizona home.

Authorities have seen an increase in tips after releasing the ransom notes that were sent to Nancy Guthrie's family.

Authorities have not confirmed the ransom notes are authentic, but their release has generated a "slight" uptick in tips, a spokeswoman for the Pima County Sheriff's Office said. The office released the full content of the alleged notes on July 31.

"Nancy Guthrie Task Force investigators have seen a slight increase in tips since the two ransom notes were released last week," Pima County Sheriff's Office Public Information Officer Angelica Carrillo told Fox News Digital. "All tips have been followed up on."

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

Nancy Guthrie, the mother of "Today" co-host Savannah Guthrie, remains missing and the family is urging renewed attention as the search drags on. (Courtesy of NBC)

The alleged ransom notes were sent on Feb. 2 and Feb. 6.

"Hello Savannah," one of the notes read. "We have your mother Nancy. She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom and once payment is received she will be released unharmed."

"She had a white smart watch on the floor of the foot of her bed and the white flood light in backyard was destroyed," it continued.

In a follow-up message sent to the Guthrie family, the alleged ransom notes states that Nancy Guthrie has passed away.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Savannah Guthrie poses alongside her mother Nancy Guthrie during a production break whilst hosting NBC's "Today Show" live from Australia. (Photo by Don Arnold/WireImage)

"We did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related," the purported ransom note states.

As previously noted, Fox News Digital has not independently verified the authenticity of the notes or their contents.

The first purported Nancy Guthrie ransom demand was sent on Feb. 2, a day after her suspected abduction in Tucson, according to authorities.

The second message was sent on Feb. 6, and authorities say it shares the same "unique linguistic style" as the original ransom demand.

Fox News Digital learned of the watch on the morning of Tuesday, Feb. 3, a day after the note was sent, according to authorities. That timeline suggests the sender knew about the watch before the detail became public.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Jason Pack, a retired FBI negotiator, said the watch detail demonstrates familiarity with the house but not necessarily knowledge unique to Guthrie or proof that she was alive.

This image released by the FBI shows an armed individual who appears to have a light emitting from his mouth at Nancy Guthrie's front door the morning of her disappearance in Tucson, Arizona, Sunday, February 1, 2026. (Provided by FBI)

"He knew about the watch on the floor — almost nobody did," Pack said. "In my view, two things the language does support: He writes like a native English speaker. The idiom and the small connecting words are all in the right places, and at this length that is hard to fake."

Anyone with information is asked to call 1-800-CALL-FBI, or 520-88-CRIME to remain anonymous.

Adam Sabes is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Adam.Sabes@fox.com and on Twitter @asabes10.

articles.title: Two civilians killed in Houthi strike on Marib, says Yemen’s government
articles.excerpt:
At least two civilians have been killed and 14 injured in the latest Houthi attack on the Yemeni government-held city of Marib, according to the internationally recognised government.

Qassem Bahaibah...
articles.body_text:
At least two civilians have been killed and 14 injured in the latest Houthi attack on the Yemeni government-held city of Marib, according to the internationally recognised government.

Qassem Bahaibah, Yemen’s health minister, denounced the Iran-aligned Houthis as a “terrorist militia” in a post on X on Friday, adding that the toll of casualties was preliminary.

Bahaibah said authorities had instructed all health facilities to raise their levels of alert and preparedness.

Friday’s attacks came the day after the Houthis killed at least 30 government soldiers in Hadramout and Marib provinces.

The government condemned Friday’s attack “in the strongest terms”, in a media statement issued by the Ministry of Public Health and Population.

“The deliberate targeting of safe residential neighbourhoods and camps of displaced people, and the resulting casualties among unarmed civilians, constitutes a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law and of all humanitarian values and covenants,” it said.

“It places the international community and humanitarian and human-rights organisations before their responsibilities, and calls for a serious and urgent stance that protects civilians and puts an end to their continued targeting.”

Marib hosts the largest number of displaced families in Yemen, according to the United Nations refugee agency.

Earlier on Friday, the Yemeni Defence Ministry said its forces had shot down several Houthi drones over Marib.

The Houthis did not immediately comment on the government’s statements.

The attacks came amid intermittent fighting on several front lines across Yemen since early July that has resulted in dozens of casualties on both sides.

The Houthis have also increased attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, following a sharp rise in tensions triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The Saudi-led coalition, which supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government, said on Friday that 11 people, including a four-year-old, were injured in a Houthi attack on the city of Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

Escalating tensions between the Houthis and Riyadh come as Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact on Friday, stating that an attack on any of the three countries would be treated as an attack on all.

The Iran-backed Houthis took control of Yemen’s capital Sanaa in 2014. Since then, they have been fighting the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government in the port city of Aden.

articles.title: 'Melrose Place' star Andrew Shue says 70% believe the American Dream is 'dead or dying'
articles.excerpt:
Melrose Place" alum Andrew Shue told Fox News Digital that economic strain, political dysfunction and anxiety about the future have left Americans feeling like the country’s "engine is broken."

Forme...
articles.body_text:
Melrose Place" alum Andrew Shue told Fox News Digital that economic strain, political dysfunction and anxiety about the future have left Americans feeling like the country’s "engine is broken."

Former "Melrose Place" star Andrew Shue believes that the majority of Americans have lost faith in the promise that once defined the country.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, the 59-year-old actor, who founded the new bipartisan initiative The Forum, shared his grim assessment of the current mood of citizens in the United States, arguing that people across the economic and political spectrum are struggling.

JOHN ADAMS MADE A TERRIFYING PREDICTION. AMERICA IS CLOSE TO PROVING HIM CORRECT

"There's nobody in this country right now that thinks we're in a good place," Shue said. "You look around and you say, how do we feel about our kids? How do we fill it feel about our kid's future? What kind of anxiety level do we all have? You're seeing 70% believe the American dream is dead or dying."

Andrew Shue became a household name on ‘Melrose Place’ (Getty Images for ADAPT Leadership Awards)

"So we're all in this boat together," he continued. "There's nobody who's jumping out, whether you're a billionaire, a bartender, everybody in between, we are all in this together."

Shue said that Americans' growing pessimism is not being driven by a single election or political figure, but by systemic problems he believes have accumulated over decades.

"We're realizing that the engine is broken and the main systems that drive that engine are our political system and our economic system," Shue explained. "The political system only rewards people in power — there happen to be a lot of old people — and performative conflict. The economic system is really just rewarding people at the top. Ninety percent feel like they're treading water or underwater, and have been for decades. The other thing I'll say is all of these problems existed long before [current U.S. President] Donald Trump came to the scene."

WATCH HERE: ‘MELROSE PLACE’ ALUM ANDREW SHUE SAYS 70% BELIEVE THE AMERICAN DREAM IS ‘DEAD OR DYING’

WORLD SERIES CHAMPION JOE GIRARDI REVEALS WHAT HE FINDS MOST 'DISTURBING' ABOUT POLITICS TODAY

"And so, as we look around, and we're fighting each other, and we try to figure out, what are we gonna do? Who's coming to save us? The answer is right in front of us," he continued. "It's us. It's the American people. The question is, ‘Oh, that seems kind of obvious. Yeah, the consent of the governed.’ We are the ones who are supposed to be the ultimate authority."

To help address what he sees as the country's growing divide, Shue founded The Forum, a nonpartisan civic initiative that brings together politically diverse Americans to identify areas of agreement and develop policy proposals. The initiative has already been implemented in three early primary states, including South Carolina, New Hampshire and Nevada.

"We have launched the Forum that I've been working on for the last eight years with an incredible team," he said. "It's the place and the process for the American people to co-create that renewal agenda. Over 300,000 people have participated so far. Perfectly politically balanced — conservatives showing up, liberals showing up, people on the far left, far right — everybody's showing up, and we have credibility and legitimacy."

Shue spent eight years founding the new bipartisan initiative The Forum to help bridge the political divide.  (Gary Gershoff/Getty Images)

"Elected leaders from both sides who put down their arms are actually leading the efforts in each state," he added. "So this is the way forward. The question is, will the legislators, the elected leaders, follow? The American people are ready to lead."

SEN CHUCK SCHUMER UNVEILS ANTI-CORRUPTION AGENCY AIMED AT TRUMP AND FUTURE PRESIDENTS

As the initiative has expanded across three states, Shue told Fox News Digital that he has been struck by how quickly participants find common ground despite their political differences.

"I think that the thing that surprised me the most was that when you give people this assignment, you say, 'It's now on you, you are going to be the hero of the story. All you have to do is work together, listen to each other, listen to your lived experiences, and come up with something that you can agree on,'" Shue said.

WATCH HERE: ‘MELROSE PLACE’ ALUM ANDREW SHUE LAUNCHES NEW BIPARTISAN INITIATIVE THE FORUM TO BREAK AMERICA'S POLITICAL GRIDLOCK

"And 70% have to agree — that's the supermajority number, 70% or higher — and then it can go forward as draft legislation," he continued. "And the thing that's beautiful is when you get these people in the rooms with people who are different, they can't figure out who the Democrat or the Republican is. They see all the common values. They see the common goal."

"Once you start listening to each other, once you start feeling like you're on the same team, and you have the same goal, anything's possible," Shue added. "And people are desperate. That's the thing. People are desperate. They're really ready for something new."

AS AMERICA MARKS 250 YEARS, OUR GREATEST CHAPTERS ARE STILL AHEAD OF US

The Delaware native also reflected on what has restored his optimism about Americans and what they can achieve when they are united.

Shue said that he remains optimistic that Americans can come together to fix the system that he described as "broken." (Scott Gries/Getty Images)

"That we know what makes America, America," he said. "It's about that confidence, that belief in what's possible. You know, I think [U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it best, 'Anyone from anywhere can become anything.' And people believe that and they live that."

"America is a place — obviously we talk about opportunity — it's a place that gives everybody a shot," Shue continued. "And this is the moment where, again, we talk about the hero. This is the moment for the American people to be the heroes."

While Shue has largely stepped away from Hollywood, he said his "Melrose Place" fame has helped shine a spotlight on The Forum.

"It certainly hasn't hurt," he said. "People are a little bit confused. And then I tell them what I've been doing for the last eight years and how committed I've been to this project."

"This provides not just the pathway to create that renewal agenda, not just a pathway to create this new power source that's going to kind of break through this partisan gridlock that we have, but it's the opportunity for everybody to be part of something," Shue explained.

WATCH HERE: ANDREW SHUE CALLS ‘MELROSE’ PLACE THE ‘ULTIMATE EXAMPLE OF THE AMERICAN DREAM’

"If you think about even MAGA and you say, why was MAGA so strong? It's because they belonged to something," he added. "But we need to belong to something that's not about beating the other side. We've got to belong to something that's about going somewhere together. We want to be on the same team. We are so exhausted with our politics."

"The American people can do this, create that renewal agenda, and then we create the power base to enforce it. And like I said, the elected leaders are going to have to go along with it because this is the only way we can do it."

Reflecting on the personal challenges he has faced in recent years, Shue said difficult experiences have changed the way he approaches relationships and community.

Shue said that he believes Americans "want to be on the same team." (Jason Mendez/Getty Images for Do Something)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"It definitely makes you try to put yourself in other people's shoes," he said. "To walk in other people's shoes is such an important part of building any kind of community, building any kind of understanding. We are all flawed. We are trying to be better people. We make decisions sometimes that don't work out for us or for our kids."

"And those experiences, when you really struggle, and you go through something painful, it teaches you what you're all about," Shue added.

As Shue now spends his time trying to help others rediscover faith in the American Dream, he said that he feels he experienced it firsthand during his own acting career when he landed his starring role on "Melrose Place."

MICRON'S $250 MILLION BET ON KIDS IS A BLUEPRINT FOR AMERICA'S FUTURE

Shue said that starring in "Melrose Place" was the "ultimate example of the American Dream." ( Fotos International/Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"It just gave me a ton of confidence," he said. "It gave me doors that were opened and it gave me a platform. And it came at a time in my life where I was a little bit trying to figure out my direction and what I was capable of. But it did give me possibility. I mean, it was the ultimate example of the American dream."

"It was a real boost to my confidence and a boost to my thought process about what could be possible."

Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

As Alex Murdaugh's road to his retrial heats up, his defense team has demanded a new evidence search in a bid to hunt for cracks in the prosecution's case.

In a Wednesday filing, Murdaugh’s attorneys argued that because several years have passed since his first trial, prosecutors should conduct a fresh search for any evidence that could help the defense or undermine the state’s witnesses.

His team also wants information that could be used to challenge a witness’s credibility, including misconduct records, disciplinary findings, inconsistent statements, plea deals, rewards or promises of favorable treatment.

MURDAUGH DEFENSE PLANS ALTERNATE SUSPECT PUSH AS DNA QUESTIONS LOOM OVER RETRIAL

Disgraced South Carolina lawyer Alex Murdaugh was convicted in March of murdering his wife, Maggie, and youngest son, Paul, on his hunting estate in June 2021. (Andrew J. Whitaker/The Post And Courier via AP, Pool, File)

The request also covers new forensic or DNA findings, additional search warrants and information related to two other SLED investigations known as the "Side of Road" and narcotics cases.

The lawyers also want written confirmation that prosecutors completed a current search and disclosed everything required.

They've asked for the information within 30 days.

Defense attorney Dick Harpootlian, right, passes documents to prosecuting attorney Creighton Waters on Monday, June 29, 2026, at a status hearing at the Marc H. State Judge Debra McCaslin oversees a status hearing involving Alex Murdaugh with prosecuting attorney Creighton Waters and defense attorney Dick Harpootlian, on Monday, June 29, 2026, at the Marc H.
