articles.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's long-lost plane reignites with ambitious new expedition
articles.excerpt:
Air and Space Museum’s Amelia Earhart expert Dorothy Cochrane speaks with Fox News Digital about the theories surrounding the famed aviator's disappearance.

Researchers are gearing up to resume their...
articles.body_text:
Air and Space Museum’s Amelia Earhart expert Dorothy Cochrane speaks with Fox News Digital about the theories surrounding the famed aviator's disappearance.

Researchers are gearing up to resume their search for Amelia Earhart's lost plane in the Pacific Ocean after setbacks delayed the search.

Purdue University officials said in a recent statement that researchers will travel to Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific to investigate the Taraia Object, a satellite-imaged anomaly believed by some to be Earhart's lost Lockheed Electra.

The expedition, called the Taraia Object Expedition, will depart on Oct. 7.

AMELIA EARHART MYSTERY EXPEDITION HALTED AS RESEARCHERS SEEK ANSWERS ON MISSING PLANE

"The expedition seeks to help complete the historic journey that ended with her disappearance 89 years ago," officials said.

The expedition is based on researchers' belief that Earhart's plane came down near Nikumaroro, known as the Nikumaroro Hypothesis.

Researchers are preparing to travel to Nikumaroro Island in October as part of a new expedition to search for the long-missing aircraft of Amelia Earhart. (U.S. National Archives)

Supporters of the theory believe that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan became stranded on the remote island after failing to reach Howland Island — possibly dying as castaways.

Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to become the first female pilot to fly around the world.

NEWLY RELEASED AMELIA EARHART DOCUMENTS REVEAL VIVID DETAILS OF JAPAN'S ROLE IN SEARCH FOR DOOMED AVIATOR

She and Noonan lost contact during one of the final legs of their journey, going missing after leaving Lae, New Guinea, en route to Howland Island.

Supporters of the Nikumaroro hypothesis believe Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan became stranded after failing to reach Howland Island. An image of Nikumaroro Island is seen above. (Google Maps)

She was 39 years old at the time and one of the most famous people in the world.

The upcoming expedition was announced last year but was delayed while officials awaited approval from the government of Kiribati. The country's cabinet has since approved the mission.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Richard Pettigrew, founder and executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute, which is leading the expedition, said that he is "grateful for the patience and enthusiasm of everyone who has followed this journey with us."

Pilot Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, are shown with a map of the Pacific that shows the planned route of their last flight. (Getty)

"The evidence supporting the Nikumaroro Hypothesis remains compelling, and the only way to answer this question is to go to Nikumaroro, inspect the Taraia Object firsthand and follow the evidence wherever it leads," Pettigrew said in a statement.

Fox News Digital reached out to Purdue University for comment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The story of Earhart's disappearance has captivated Americans for decades and has been the subject of ongoing research.

Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to become the first female pilot to fly around the world. (Getty)

Last year, the National Archives released over 4,600 pages of previously unsealed government records related to Earhart's 1937 disappearance, including her final known radio transmissions.

More recently, pilot Justin Myers said he identified a possible image of Earhart's missing Lockheed Electra in Google Earth imagery of Nikumaroro.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

articles.title: Rita Wilson ignored her mother's old-school marriage advice and it led her to Tom Hanks
articles.excerpt:
Tom Hanks and wife Rita Wilson walked the Pre-Grammy GALA red carpet discussing what they believe is the success to a great relationship, after being married for 34 years.

Rita Wilson is sharing the ...
articles.body_text:
Tom Hanks and wife Rita Wilson walked the Pre-Grammy GALA red carpet discussing what they believe is the success to a great relationship, after being married for 34 years.

Rita Wilson is sharing the marriage advice her mom gave that didn't sit right with her.

During a recent appearance on Michelle Obama's podcast, "In My Opinion," the 69-year-old actress spoke about the outdated marriage advice her mom gave her before she met and married Tom Hanks.

"I was engaged before I got engaged to my husband. If I had married that person, I would have been divorced within a year," she said. "I thought that was what you were supposed to do at a certain age. I actually thought, because I had never really fallen in love with anyone, that I would be okay."

While engaged to that man, Wilson said she asked her mom for advice, telling her: "I don't know though. Should I marry him? I'm not really in love with him," and getting a surprising response in return.

Wilson shared she was engaged prior to meeting Tom Hanks and the marriage advice her mom gave her. (Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images)

'SHAMELESS' STAR EMMY ROSSUM REVEALS SECRET MARRIAGE AT 21 AFTER BOYFRIEND'S ALLEGED SHOCKING ULTIMATUM

"She said, 'Don't worry, you grow to love him.' I was like, 'Mom, that's not my generation,'" she said. "Her generation was like, 'Is he a good man? Will he provide?' There wasn't any of this, 'I have to be madly in love.' My parents were married for 59 years, so whatever they figured out, they figured out. But I still wanted to hold out for that falling in love thing."

Ultimately, Wilson did not go through with marrying the first man, knowing "marriage would not have sustained that relationship," and found love with Hanks after they reunited on set of "Volunteers" in 1984, later tying the knot in 1988.

The "Now and Then" actress told Obama, and her co-host and brother, Craig Robinson, that when she "finally met Tom and fell in love with" Hanks, she had the feeling that "this is very, very different than what I had before."

When it comes to being a mom, Wilson said she wasn't sure she wanted to have children, but knew she "didn't wanna have children with the wrong people or person."

Wilson said seeing what a good father Hanks was encouraged her to want kids. (Dave Benett/WireImage)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"Tom had two children," she said. "I already saw that he could be a good dad. So I was like, okay, good, that's helpful. A little example here."

Hanks was already a father to Colin and Elizabeth, who he shares with his ex-wife, Samantha Lewes, and later welcomed sons Chet and Truman with Wilson.

Of his children, Colin and Chet have followed in Hanks and Wilson's footsteps, with Elizabeth pursuing a career and an author and journalist, under the pen name E.A. Hanks, and Truman focusing on other aspects of filmmaking.

Most recently, Chet has found success starring in "Running Point" alongside Kate Hudson, and Colin has appeared in a number of successful projects, including "Life In Pieces," "Fargo," "American Crime Story" and others.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Chet Hanks shared that he asks his dad for career advice all the time. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)

"I’ve always asked him for advice when it comes to acting and he’s always given me really great advice," Chet told Page Six in September 2024. "He just said, ‘If you just know your lines, and you show up on time, and you’re nice to everybody, that gets you a long way.'"

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Viagra could do more than advertised as study reveals surprising health superpower
articles.excerpt: Dr. Loren Rourke, a Texas-based board-certified breast cancer surgeon, author and speaker, confirmed research has suggested that glucagon-like peptide-1 medications — including Ozempic and Wegovy — ma...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Loren Rourke, a Texas-based board-certified breast cancer surgeon, author and speaker, confirmed research has suggested that glucagon-like peptide-1 medications — including Ozempic and Wegovy — may be associated with a lower risk of cancer recurrence and potentially new diagnoses.

Viagra could do more than give men a boost in the bedroom, as new research suggests it may have benefits for cancer patients.

The prescription medication, which is manufactured and distributed by Viatris, is commonly used to treat erectile dysfunction by increasing blood flow during sexual stimulation.

It was originally developed to treat high blood pressure and chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart before researchers discovered its unexpected effect on erectile function during clinical trials.

PANCREATIC CANCER VACCINE SHOWS PROMISE IN FIRST HUMAN TRIAL, PREVENTING DISEASE IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS

A new study published by the American Association for Cancer Research found that the pill may have properties that can prevent cancer from spreading.

Researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, led by Dr. Yarden Ariav in the lab of Professor Ayelet Erez, found that Viagra’s active ingredient — sildenafil, a PDE5 inhibitor — may restrict cancer metastasis, or the formation of new tumors.

Viagra’s active ingredient, sildenafil, may restrict cancer cells from spreading, a new study suggests.

The team, which included scientists at the U.S. National Cancer Institute, analyzed human and mouse cancer cells, genetic experiments and 20 years of health data from five million members of Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest nonprofit healthcare provider and health insurer. They also examined how genes, proteins, fats, cholesterol and cellular energy interact.

The analysis revealed that sildenafil limits the cancer cell’s ability to make use of cholesterol, which is an important mechanism in how the cell breaks away from the primary tumor and migrates throughout the body, according to a press release from the American Committee for the Weizmann Institute of Science.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sildenafil was found to block an enzyme called phosphodiesterase type 5, or PDE5, and increase the signaling molecule called cGMP, which dilates blood vessels – the feature that has made Viagra a successful treatment for erectile dysfunction.

According to the researchers, cGMP also binds to a protein that transports cholesterol within cells, reducing the cholesterol available for essential cellular functions. Cancer cells are "particularly vulnerable to this reduction in cholesterol supply," they noted.

Viagra was originally developed to treat high blood pressure and chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart before researchers discovered its unexpected effect on erectile function during clinical trials. (Alex Segre/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Based on their findings, the researchers suggested that combining Viagra-related drugs with statins, which lower cholesterol, could help slow the spread of cancer by reducing tumor cells' access to both existing and newly produced cholesterol.

"We have uncovered a new biological pathway that links a well-known signaling molecule to cholesterol regulation within cells and shown how this pathway can be harnessed to interfere with the ability of cancer cells to form metastases," Erez, senior researcher and dean of Weizmann’s Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, commented in a statement.

Combining drugs from the Viagra family with statins – a class of drugs responsible for reducing cholesterol production in the body – may be even more effective in restricting the spread of cancer, the researchers suggested. (iStock)

"Beyond their therapeutic promise, our findings highlight that cancer biology is shaped not only by mutations in tumor cells, but also by the patient’s metabolic state and by medications they are already taking for other conditions."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The researcher added that this study "underscores the importance of treating the whole patient – not just the cancer – when tailoring the most effective therapy."

The study’s use of mouse models could pose a limitation to the final implications, as cancer treatment may not always translate similarly to humans, the researchers acknowledged.

The human evidence is also observational, which reveals an association instead of a proven cause and effect.

Fox News Digital reached out to the study authors and the medication's manufacturer for comment.

Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Senate confirms Trump pick Erica Schwartz as new CDC director
articles.excerpt:
Schwartz, president’s third pick to lead top US public health agency, confirmed in 51-44 Senate vote

Dr Erica Schwartz was confirmed by the US Senate as director ‌of the Centers for Disease Control a...
articles.body_text:
Schwartz, president’s third pick to lead top US public health agency, confirmed in 51-44 Senate vote

Dr Erica Schwartz was confirmed by the US Senate as director ‌of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), a rare win for the Trump administration after a string of failed attempts to fill senior health posts.

Schwartz was confirmed by a ⁠51-44 vote that broke largely along party lines, with Tim Kaine of Virginia the sole Democrat to support her nomination.

Donald Trump’s third pick to run ​the CDC, Schwartz is set to take the reins of the agency after a tumultuous period of leadership turnover, and amid public concern over an outbreak of cyclosporiasis and Robert F Kennedy Jr’s hesitancy towards vaccines.

At her confirmation hearing last month, senators pressed Schwartz on whether she would stand firm against any attempts by the health secretary to erode the scientific consensus around vaccines. She replied that she “will never betray the science” but generally deflected questions about how she would manage the relationship with Kennedy.

“We need a CDC director that will ⁠actually stand up to crazy, stupid things being said that undermine faith in immunization,” said Bill Cassidy, the committee’s Republican chair and a physician.

Schwartz replied that Kennedy “will absolutely allow me to be CDC director”, and Cassidy later announced his support for her nomination.

“There are challenges facing Americans’ health today. I will work with her to face those challenges and regain trust in the CDC,” Cassidy said after the Senate confirmed her.

A navy veteran, Schwartz served as deputy surgeon general during Trump’s first term, after positions in the United States Public Health Service where she was detailed to the Coast Guard, eventually becoming the force’s chief medical officer.

Trump’s first nominee to lead the CDC, David Weldon, a former Florida congressman, was withdrawn by the White House in March 2025 just before his confirmation hearing.

Schwartz will be the first permanent CDC ​director since Susan Monarez, Trump’s second pick, who was fired by Kennedy last year after less than a month over a clash on vaccine policy.

articles.title: Fauci slapped with subpoena as COVID doc probed for 'profiting' off federal guidance
articles.excerpt: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier joins John Roberts to discuss launching an investigation and sending a subpoena to Dr. Anthony Fauci. This development comes as a Senate panel prepares to vote ...
articles.body_text:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier joins John Roberts to discuss launching an investigation and sending a subpoena to Dr. Anthony Fauci. This development comes as a Senate panel prepares to vote on a contempt resolution after Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times during recent Capitol Hill testimony regarding the origins of COVID-19.

FIRST ON FOX: A top Florida official is slapping Anthony Fauci with a subpoena over alleged "profiting" from federal guidance that hurt businesses, residents.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Wednesday he has issued an investigative subpoena against former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Disease Director Anthony Fauci.

The subpoena is part of a state probe into Fauci’s awards, incentives and guidance that impacted Florida’s residents and their businesses during the coronavirus pandemic.

FAUCI'S FIFTH FUELS VOW TO HAUL HIM INTO COURT 'EVERY DAY' DESPITE BIDEN PARDON

A split of Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier and former NIAID Director Anthony Fauci (Dominic Gwinn/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images; Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The announcement comes after Uthmeier, along with Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., pledged to have Fauci investigated at the state level following his Senate Homeland Security and Government Affairs Committee hearing last week when he pleaded the Fifth 111 times and references were made to his blanket federal pardon from former President Joe Biden.

"We issued a formal subpoena to Dr. Fauci under Florida state law, seeking a breadth of documents ranging to what he knew when he knew it, his doubts about the safety and efficacy of vaccines that he's out there promoting, and we're really focused in on his self-dealing," Uthmeier announced on Fox News.

"Evidence has come to light that he was trying to personally profit off of this. This is outside of his government duties, his official role: He's trying to pursue book deals, awards, get connected with high rollers that might help him come into millions and millions of dollars. This is wrong, and it could go towards a deceptive trade practice, fraud, public nuisance, you name it. I think there's many aspects of Florida law that now are implicated."

Uthmeier said the activities he is being subpoenaed over were revealed largely through his diary – several hundred pages of writings made on a federal server that Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., released last week.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Former NIH Director Anthony Fauci listens during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on July 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Fauci declined to answer questions, asserting his Fifth Amendment right. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"We know one award in particular, he made $900,000 on that," he said, appearing to refer to Fauci receiving approximately that amount from the Dan David Prize from Tel Aviv University.

Uthmeier said that when a bureaucrat is issuing directives and mandates he is privately questioning while also deriving a profit from that work, it raises legal questions.

"It starts as a civil inquiry," Uthmeier said. "But we're going to tie in all aspects of Florida common law, things ranging from deceptive trade, fraud, public nuisance, nothing is off the table."

The subpoena asks for awards Fauci applied to, considered or received from any organization, including those within the state of Florida, relating to the pandemic.

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

Anthony Fauci declined to testify in a Senate committee hearing on his role in the US response to Covid-19, invoking his 5th Amendment rights. (Left (Alex WROBLEWSKI / AFP via Getty Images), Right (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images))

It also asks for information on professional opportunities offered to or considered by Fauci, as well as interactions and communications with Florida businesses, media outlets and communities regarding COVID-19 vaccination sites, social distancing and mask orders, and school closures.

A pair of other states expressed encouragement at the news.

West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey alleged Fauci’s refusal to answer Paul’s questions is "concerning" and that the American people deserve to know whether they were misled or "manipulated."

"Both my Office and I support Attorney General Uthmeier’s efforts to uncover the truth," McCuskey said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill added that the public "deserves answers to about a million questions related to the pandemic, its origins, and the government’s actions in response."

Murrill alleged Fauci had lied and said that "we just don’t know how much" so.

"But he lied about something as basic as keeping a diary. The truth will come out."

Fox News Digital reached out to Schertler Law, counsel for Fauci, for comment.

Fox News Digital’s Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

articles.title: Judge tosses Alex Murdaugh’s $600,000 suit against former court clerk
articles.excerpt:
Murdaugh, whose murder convictions were overturned due to clerk’s misconduct, will face trial again

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by A...
articles.body_text:
Murdaugh, whose murder convictions were overturned due to clerk’s misconduct, will face trial again

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by Alex Murdaugh seeking $600,000 in legal fees from the former court clerk whose misconduct led to his murder convictions being overturned on appeal.

Murdaugh sued Becky Hill in May, saying she violated his right to a fair trial over the deaths of his wife and son.

A jury found Murdaugh guilty, but the state supreme court overturned the convictions and life sentences earlier this year, saying Hill’s comments to jurors suggested the once-prominent lawyer was guilty and his testimony in his own defense could not be trusted.

The problem with Murdaugh’s legal reasoning is he would have had to spend the money anyway, because it was not Hill who investigated or pursued justice against him, Judge Richard Gergel wrote in his ruling on Wednesday.

“Plaintiff’s claim contains a fatal flaw – the lack of a causal connection between the funds he expended for his defense in the first trial and defendant’s misconduct. Defendant had no role in the initiation of criminal charges against plaintiff,” Gergel wrote.

Murdaugh said in court papers he spent $600,000 from a retirement account to pay for his lawyers in his first trial and will need more money to pay them for his retrial next year in the case that has become a true crime sensation with a streaming miniseries, bestselling books and dozens of podcasts.

Even with his murder convictions overturned, Murdaugh remains in prison. He pleaded guilty to stealing about $12m from his clients and is serving a 40-year federal sentence at the same time as a 27-year state sentence for his financial crimes.

His retrial on the murder charges has been scheduled for April.

Investigators said Murdaugh was addicted to opioids and his complex schemes to steal money from clients and his family’s law firm were starting to unravel so he killed his wife and son to divert attention and buy time to find a way out of his problems.

articles.title: Terrifying 'human safaris' on display in shocking video that reveals depths of Russia's deadly campaign
articles.excerpt: Video released by the Kherson Regional Military Administration appears to show a drone following a man at a market in southern Ukraine before detonating near him, the 52-year-old civilian was injured ...
articles.body_text:
Video released by the Kherson Regional Military Administration appears to show a drone following a man at a market in southern Ukraine before detonating near him, the 52-year-old civilian was injured in the Aug. 4 attack. (Credit: Reuters)

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of going "mad" following the release of a video showing a Ukrainian vegetable vendor being stalked by a Russian military drone before the drone exploded near him.

The incident occurred on Aug. 4 at a Kherson market located in Southern Ukraine. Footage released by the Kherson Regional Military Administration shows a drone hovering near a man standing beside a minibus before following him as he moves behind the bus. Moments later the drone dives toward the minibus and explodes near its front, detonating close to where the man is standing.

"A Russian drone deliberately hunted down a man selling vegetables and detonated right next to him," Zelenskyy wrote on X in a post including the video. "The Russians even admitted to the crime, showing zero regret and openly boasting about tormenting people. The man was wounded in the blast. Every single day, ordinary people in Kherson face these Russian "safaris."

MOSCOW BOMBING EXPOSES POTENTIAL SECURITY GAPS AROUND PUTIN'S MILITARY ELITE, EXPERT SAYS

Zelenskyy sat down with Fox News for a wide-ranging interview, outlining how Ukraine’s war-time innovations are now shaping global defense partnerships. (Fox News)

The street vendor, identified as 52-year-old Yuriy, survived the near-fatal encounter, which Ukrainian authorities describe as part of a pattern of Russian drone attacks that track and target civilians — a practice they have dubbed "human safaris."

Speaking from a hospital bed, Yuriy told BBC that he and his wife were setting up their stall when he heard the drone buzzing nearby. His wife had run away, and the drone zeroed in on Yuriy, who pulled out vegetables to show that he did not have a weapon.

"It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yuriy told BBC. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attack a "barbaric war crime," demanding international intervention.

WHY TRUMP IS DOWNPLAYING REPORTS RUSSIA AND CHINA ARE HELPING IRAN

Zelenskyy argued that everyone should see the video to make clear what Russia is capable of, arguing that President Vladimir Putin won't stop with Ukraine.

"This is not just about Ukraine," Zelenskyy wrote. "Russia’s campaign against human life must be stopped here in Ukraine before it spreads further. Finland and Kazakhstan, the Baltic states and Poland, the countries of the South Caucasus, Romania, and Moldova — all should work together to ensure real security guarantees and bring Russia’s war to an end."

Russian drone strike killed at least 12 Ukrainian coal miners and injured seven others when it hit a civilian bus in Dnipropetrovsk region. (State Emergency Service of Ukraine, Dnipropetrovsk region)

"Peace is needed, which requires cooperation among everyone in the world who truly values peace," Zelenskyy wrote.

Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office says authorities have opened 5,303 criminal cases into drone attacks on civilian targets in the Kherson region. The office says the attacks have killed 287 civilians and wounded 2,549 others, including 41 children.

UKRAINE SEEKS MORE U.S. PATRIOT INTERCEPTORS AS BOMB SHELTER PROBE DEEPENS

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks at a podium split with an image of Russian President Vladimir Putin crossing himself at Orthodox Easter service. (Inquam Photos/Octav Ganea via Reuters; AP Photo/Alexander Zemlianichenko, Pool)

Prosecutors said the attacks appeared to be part of a systematic campaign, with FPV drones repeatedly striking civilians in public places, homes, transport hubs and civilian vehicles, and in some cases launching follow-up attacks after emergency crews arrived.

The release of the chilling video comes a year after a one-year-old boy was killed by a Russian drone in the Kherson region while playing in his playpen in his grandmother's backyard.

Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

articles.title: Republican who withdrew last month beats Trump-backed rival in Michigan
articles.excerpt:
Thomas Smith, whose name remained on ballot, beats Republican rivals in primary contest for eighth district

Thomas Smith withdrew from the Republican primary contest for Michigan’s eighth district la...
articles.body_text:
Thomas Smith, whose name remained on ballot, beats Republican rivals in primary contest for eighth district

Thomas Smith withdrew from the Republican primary contest for Michigan’s eighth district last month. On Tuesday, he won the nomination.

Unofficial results show Smith with more than 50% of the vote, according to the Associated Press, defeating the man he endorsed, anti-abortion activist Al Lemmo, and the man Donald Trump endorsed, former federal law enforcement officer Amir Hassan.

In a statement on Wednesday, Smith said he was “humbled and honored that Republicans have chosen me to take the fight to Kristen McDonald Rivet”, the Democratic incumbent in the battleground House district.

“I look forward to working with Speaker [Mike] Johnson and the entire Republican team to expand our House majority and advance President Trump’s ‘America first’ agenda to lower costs for working families and make America affordable again,” he added.

In June, Trump endorsed Hassan, an African American navy veteran who worked for the Departments of Defense, Homeland Security and Transportation. The president also appeared with Hassan at a campaign event in Michigan. Hassan said during his campaign that he had recently converted to Christianity from Islam. Nonetheless, social media commentary suggests Republican voters did not view Hassan’s conversion as authentic and were apprehensive about nominating a Muslim candidate.

“It was a tough race, but over the last year I’ve had some incredible dealings with people across the entire district,” Hassan said in a video posted to X and Facebook. “The biggest conservative value is that we don’t make excuses.”

Smith, who did little campaigning, posted on social media in July to endorse Lemmo, describing Hassan as a crypto-Republican. In Michigan, a US House candidate must withdraw their candidacy before 24 April for election officials to have enough time to remove their name from ballots.

The Federal Election Commission has no electronic campaign finance filings from Smith. It does have a handwritten letter dated 12 July declaring $1,850 in fundraising.

“I could not file this electronically because I have had no success logging in and have not been able to get a response from the helpdesk,” Smith wrote in a postscript on the letter.

The Flint native and retired General Motors engineer made a brief appearance at a Republican unity event hosted in Macomb county by the party’s newly minted US Senate candidate Mike Rogers. Smith said he intended to “unseat communist comrade Rivet”.

Though the victory on Tuesday of Abdul El-Sayed in the Democratic Senate primary has drawn national attention to progressive politics in Michigan, Rivet has signaled her relative moderation as one of 10 House Democrats to join Promise to America, a congressional initiative led by US representatives Tom Suozzi of New York and Adam Gray of California explicitly embracing capitalism and rejecting socialism.

The congressional district along Michigan’s Saginaw River, connecting Flint to the Saginaw Bay, was one of 13 districts nationwide that voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election while also electing a Democratic representative to Congress.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham calls out WNBA media for non-basketball focus, and talks viral Cheryl Reeve conversation
articles.excerpt: Former athlete Payton McNabb and columnist Dustin Grage slam Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve for wearing a controversial transgender advocacy shirt during a game. McNabb argues that political d...
articles.body_text:
Former athlete Payton McNabb and columnist Dustin Grage slam Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve for wearing a controversial transgender advocacy shirt during a game. McNabb argues that political displays overshadow female sports achievements. The discussion follows intense clashes between trans activists and supporters of WNBA star Sophie Cunningham outside a Minneapolis arena.

Sophie Cunningham said of the WNBA media "all we ever do is cover everything except basketball," while speaking to reporters on Wednesday.

"The WNBA media, all we ever do is cover everything except basketball," Cunningham said. "You can talk about other things, those are great stories, it shows fans who people (are) outside of the court, but I think we gotta keep the main thing the main thing."

Cunningham's comments come after being at the center of a national media firestorm for weeks, after an ESPN article reported quotes in which she expressed support for the protection of women's sports. Cunningham claimed the interview for that piece happened earlier this year.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham reacts to game action against the Portland Fire during the first half at Moda Center in Portland, Ore., on July 31, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

"I want to get back to basketball," Cunningham said. "I just want to make sure that the focus stays where it should because people are playing at such a high level."

Cunningham's public stance on the issue has prompted rallies at the Fever's last three games, with two more rallies scheduled for their game in Chicago against the Sky on Saturday, and their game in New York against the Liberty on Aug. 22. The rallies have thrust the entire WNBA into the national debate over the issue of trans athletes in women's sports, as four coaches have gone on record with statements about the issue since the rallies began.

At the Fever's most recent game against the Minnesota Lynx, Cunningham was seen having an intense conversation with Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, who was wearing a "trans kids belong" shirt.

"Yeah, she just came up and I respect her for coming up in person," Cunningham said Wednesday of the conversation. "I think a lot of people hide behind screens and love that type of thing.

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

Sophie Cunningham No. 8 of the Indiana Fever warms up before a game against the Seattle Storm at Climate Pledge Arena on July 28, 2026, in Seattle, Wash. (Soobum Im/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"She had stories about her point of view and I had stories about my point of view and we left with love and respect and I think that’s what it’s all about."

Meanwhile, the Fever, currently navigating a crucial stretch of their 2026 campaign following a hard-fought 108-100 loss to the Lynx on Aug. 2, have largely attempted to shield their locker room from the national conversation.

Superstar Caitlin Clark faced a question about the rallies after the Lynx loss, and declined to reveal her stance on the issue.

"I think, for us, it's not really a discussion we really have in our locker room," Clark answered. "I think it's for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. Our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and, obviously, we didn't do that tonight. So we need to find an area to improve in that way."

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Clark then declined a related follow-up question, saying "I just answered for you."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

At the Fever's game against the Portland Fire on Friday, after head coach Stephanie White was asked about the issue in the pre-game news conference, Clark was not made available to reporters despite recording a triple-double. Then, when a reporter sent by OutKick attempted to ask a question about Cunningham to players who were available, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson, both players fled the podium as the news conference was abruptly ended right there.

Riley Gaines, Sophie Cunningham, and XX-XY Athletics founder Jen Sey pose courtside after an Indiana Fever game with a sign thanking Cunningham. (Riley Gaines/XX-XY Athletics)

The Fever now look ahead to a high-stakes matchup against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces on Thursday, before their weekend clash with the Sky, as another rally in support of Cunningham set to take place at that game.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Getting busted hooking up in a bar's bathroom is enough of a mood killer, you don't need to assault a manager

The mood is already ruined after you get busted hooking up in a ba...
articles.body_text:
Armando Salguero explains that the NFL will continue to give talented players chances because teams think they can fix the problems.

The mood is already ruined after you get busted hooking up in a bar's bathroom. There's no need to make matters worse for yourself, especially if there's any chance you can pick back up where you left off later on.

I think that's something most people can agree on. As a matter of fact, I assumed that was one of those unwritten rules everyone was aware of. You tried and failed to get away with a romantic encounter in a bar's bathroom.

A woman allegedly busted hooking up in a bar bathroom was arrested after spitting on the manager while being escorted out. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

It's unfortunate, but it does happen. But you move on. The whole night doesn’t have to be ruined because of it. If you're being escorted out of the bar and being sent on your way, take it. That's a sign all is not lost.

DITCHING HIS 'WHIZZINATOR' IN A PATROL CAR WAS FLORIDA MAN'S SECOND BAD DECISION OF DAY

That's a piece of advice that 19-year-old Hayley Serball could have evidently used last Saturday morning at a bar/restaurant in St. Petersburg, Florida. She allegedly had sex in the bathroom then spit on the manager.

Police say she was "confronted for having sexual intercourse in a bathroom" by employees of Shiso Crispy, reports The Smoking Gun.

Florida woman ends up taking a trip to jail after she allegedly spit on the manager of a bar she was busted hooking up in. (Getty Images)

As she was been escorted from the property, she allegedly turned around and spit on the manager, Kaleena Conklin's face.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

It was noted by officers that "The spit was visible on the victim's face, and there were numerous witnesses of this."

I'd like to think there's a chance that she thought the move would restore the mood. I don’t know how or why, but I want to be as charitable as possible.

A Florida woman was allegedly caught hooking up in the bathroom at a bar and made things a lot worse for herself by spitting on the manager. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

In any event, it didn't work. Serball was arrested on a misdemeanor battery charge and later released on $1,000 bond.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

TSG reports that this isn't her first encounter with law enforcement and that she is currently a defendant in two pending felony cases.

One case stemmed from an auto burglary arrest and the other for an arrest for being an accessory after the fact to an aggravated assault with a firearm.

articles.title: SEE IT: Michigan Dem predicts far-left El-Sayed will win Senate race after backing his primary rival
articles.excerpt: Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., told Fox News Digital that Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed will beat Republican nominee Mike Rogers in November's midterms, despite backing Democratic riva...
articles.body_text:
Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., told Fox News Digital that Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed will beat Republican nominee Mike Rogers in November's midterms, despite backing Democratic rival as successor. (Credit: Fox News Digital)

Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., is confident that far-left Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed will defeat Republican nominee Mike Rogers in the race to replace him in the Senate, despite having endorsed El-Sayed’s primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens.

El-Sayed, known as a progressive insurgent, will go head-to-head with Michigan’s Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers in the upcoming midterm elections. El-Sayed’s victory marks yet another win for the left-wing Democrats in this year’s primaries that have been battling to defeat the current Democratic establishment.

"I think if you look at the issues broadly, the differences between Abdul El-Sayed and Rogers when it comes to fighting for families in Michigan, it's pretty broad," Peters said to Fox News Digital when asked if his far-left positions could give Republicans a boost in Michigan.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, films a social media video at a pool party for content creators supporting his campaign, Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

He continued, "And in the end, that's why he will prevail."

Peters’ endorsement of Stevens over El-Sayed was part of a broader effort by mainstream Democrats to beat another progressive candidate, as Republicans largely viewed El-Sayed winning as a boost for their party’s chances to flip Michigan’s Senate seat. Rogers told Fox News Digital in an interview prior to the primary results that he would "beat either one of those candidates," but that El-Sayed has "his own special sauce of crazy."

The race between Stevens and El-Sayed was strenuous as it became a determining factor of whether Democrats could win the majority back in the Senate. More than $80 million was poured into this primary, qualifying it as the most expensive Democratic Senate nomination race in history.

DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE

Rep. Haley Stevens and former public health official Abdul El-Sayed competed for the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Michigan. (Scott Olson/Getty Images; Finn Gomez/Getty Images)

Republicans have speculated that the turn to nominating Democratic socialist candidates indicates that the current Democratic establishment is losing its grip in these congressional races.

Peters pushed back on this claim, arguing that the results aren’t reflective of the entire party as this is "nothing new" for the state.

"Michigan is a very diverse state, and if you recall, Bernie Sanders beat Hillary Clinton many years ago in a primary in Michigan, so this is nothing new," Peters said, referring to the state's 2016 Democratic presidential primary.

Sanders, I-Vt., endorsed El-Sayed in his Senate primary to defeat Stevens.

HASAN PIKER UNLOADS ON 'ISLAMOPHOBIC PIECES OF S---' DEMOCRATS AS EL-SAYED FACES PARTY UNITY TEST

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate primary candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Sen. Bernie Sanders greet the crowd during a campaign rally on July 18, 2026, in Detroit. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images)

El-Sayed, a former Wayne County Health Department director, would be the first Muslim senator. He has called for defunding the police and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He is also a strong critic of Israel, labeling the country’s actions as genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

Peters declined to weigh in on where he falls on El-Sayed's policy positions — like defunding the police — despite expressing confidence the Democratic nominee will defeat Rogers.

"I'm not on the ballot, so I don't have to make those kinds of statements," Peters said.

El-Sayed and Rogers, who ran uncontested in his primary, will compete for the swing state’s Senate seat on Nov. 3 in midterm elections.

Fox News Digital’s Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Cambridge professor Jason Arday resigns amid accusations of plagiarism
articles.excerpt:
Sociology professor to stand down after university announces investigation into his qualifications and career

Playbooks, plagiarism and a pig’s head: the claims surrounding a star Cambridge professor...
articles.body_text:
Sociology professor to stand down after university announces investigation into his qualifications and career

Playbooks, plagiarism and a pig’s head: the claims surrounding a star Cambridge professor

Jason Arday, the Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism and embellishment, has resigned after the university announced he was to face new investigations into his qualifications and career.

Arday, who had been dogged by a growing series of questions over his academic work and credentials, issued a statement on Wednesday night, saying the “relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love”.

In the statement, published on the Good Law Project website, he wrote: “It is with profound sadness that I write to resign, with immediate effect, from my position at the University of Cambridge and Jesus College.

“When I accepted the extraordinary honour of becoming professor of sociology at Cambridge, it was, without question, the greatest professional privilege of my life.”

However, after days of detailed scrutiny of his previous work and statements, which highlighted apparent discrepancies, Arday said he had “concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away”.

Simon & Schuster had been preparing to publish Arday’s memoir, entitled Great and Unfortunate Things, later this month. His resignation may pause or even halt its publication and planned publicity tours.

Cambridge had initially defended Arday – the youngest black professor appointed in the university’s history, with a compelling life story of educational disadvantage – as “the victim of a vile campaign”. But as questions multiplied over Arday’s own claims, the university’s leaders felt that Cambridge’s reputation was in danger.

The Guardian published its own investigation uncovering discrepancies in Arday’s public accounts involving prodigious fundraising feats as well as claims he had been targeted by knife-wielding masked intruders.

Arday first faced allegations that he plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis and other academic research late last year, and has rejected the claims. An investigation by Liverpool John Moores University, which awarded his PhD in 2015, did not uphold the charges of plagiarism but said they were probably caused by “honest and reasonable error”.

Arday has denied all accusations of plagarism, telling the Guardian last week: “There have been multiple thorough investigations across several institutions as a result of the allegations, and immense scrutiny, including with an academic misconduct panel who concluded that there was no plagiarism or academic misconduct.”

On Wednesday evening, Cambridge announced it would launch an investigation after it said it received “new information” about his qualifications and career.

It said in a statement: “The University of Cambridge has begun an investigation following new information about Prof Arday’s academic qualifications and honorary appointments. In order to ensure a fair process, we will not comment further until this has concluded.

“Separately, there remains a number of ongoing complaints regarding academic misconduct, which are being handled in line with our misconduct in research policy. This is consistent with our previous statement on the matter.

“While we are fully aware of the public commentary and concerns around this matter, it remains vital that any process is thorough and adheres to both university policies and employment law.

“We also fully recognise that there is a person at the centre of this situation, and we continue to provide support to him.”

A spokesperson for Jesus College, Cambridge, said it was launching its own parallel “process”.

“Prof Arday’s college fellowship is linked to his university role and we will fully support the university.

“Prof Arday remains a fellow during this process. We recognise that this is a very difficult time for him and his family, and ask that they are treated with compassion and respect.”

The new investigations may have been triggered by Arday’s claims that he held a string of prestigious visiting fellowships and professorships at other universities, including statements in published biographies dating back to 2018 that he was a visiting fellow or visiting professor at Ohio State University in the US. Ohio State has denied that Arday was ever employed in any role.

Biographies linked to Arday have also claimed he had visiting professorships at Durham, Glasgow, Coventry and London Metropolitan universities as well as Nelson Mandela University in South Africa.

Arday’s appointment as professor of sociology at Cambridge, at the comparatively young age of 37, received wide publicity through Arday’s life story, which includes a diagnosis of autism at the age of three, being unable to speak until he was 11, or read or write until he was 18.

Despite those factors, Arday went on to university and swiftly climbed the academic ladder. After receiving his PhD in 2015 he held academic posts at Leeds Beckett, Roehampton and Durham universities, including a brief stint at Warwick University, before being appointed professor of sociology of education at Glasgow University in 2021. By early 2023 he had sought and won appointment to a professorship at Cambridge.

Arday also claimed to have completed 30 marathons in 35 days as well as running 600 miles in six days, and raising £5m for charity over several years. After facing questions he revised some of those claims, and instead said he was part of a funding raising group that he cannot name for legal reasons.

Arday told the Guardian he had been the target of multiple threats after his Cambridge appointment, including having a severed pig’s head delivered to his parents’ home. Subsequent investigations found no evidence to support this claim.

It is with profound sadness that I write to resign, with immediate effect, from my position at the University of Cambridge and Jesus College.

When I accepted the extraordinary honour of becoming Professor of Sociology at Cambridge, it was, without question, the greatest professional privilege of my life. To become the youngest Black professor in the University’s history was something I could scarcely have imagined as a child growing up with a diagnosis of autism, unable to speak until I was eleven years old.

The response from so many people across the world was overwhelming. Thousands celebrated not simply my appointment, but what it represented: that talent, perseverance and hope can triumph over even the greatest adversity. It has been the privilege of my life to teach my students, to learn alongside them, and to witness their curiosity, kindness and ambition. They have given me far more than I could ever have given them.

Sadly, the years since my appointment have also been marked by an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack. While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement. The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love.

I have tried to continue because I believe deeply in the values of higher education, in rigorous scholarship, and in the transformative power of universities. I have tried because of my students, my colleagues and the countless people who have written to tell me that my journey gave them hope.

But there comes a point when the personal cost becomes too great.

I have a family. I want to be present for them. I want to reclaim some peace, some privacy and some semblance of an ordinary life. I no longer wish to feel as though I am living under a constant spotlight, where every aspect of my life is subject to public examination and judgement.

For my own wellbeing, for my family, and for those who have stood by me throughout this difficult period, I have concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away.

This decision should not be interpreted as a loss of faith in scholarship or in the values that first brought me to Cambridge. Nor should it be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me. It is simply the decision of someone who has reached the limits of what any person should reasonably be expected to endure.

To my students: thank you. Teaching you has been the greatest honour of my academic career. Your brilliance, compassion and determination give me enormous hope for the future.

To my colleagues and to the many thousands of people, from every corner of the world, who have supported me, defended me, written to me, and believed in me when it mattered most, I offer my deepest gratitude. Your kindness has carried me through some of the darkest moments of my life.

This is not the end of my work. It is simply the end of this chapter.

I need time to heal. I need time to simply be myself again.

I will return stronger, wiser and with the same determination that has always defined my journey. There is still so much work to do, and I look forward to doing it alongside so many of you in the years ahead.

For now, however, I ask only for understanding, for compassion, and for the space to begin again.

articles.title: ‘Disturbing’: TikTok faces criticism after Perez Hilton livestreams self-harm
articles.excerpt:
Many online questioned how long the blogger’s broadcast remained up on the app and shared mental health resources

Social media users have criticized TikTok after the celebrity blogger Perez Hilton li...
articles.body_text:
Many online questioned how long the blogger’s broadcast remained up on the app and shared mental health resources

Social media users have criticized TikTok after the celebrity blogger Perez Hilton livestreamed himself self-harming on the platform, prompting many to question how long the broadcast remained live and others to share mental health resources and encourage those in need to seek help.

On Tuesday night, Hilton, 48, livestreamed himself engaging in self-harm as viewers pleaded for him to stop. Shortly after, local authorities responded to his home in Miami, Florida, where he was transported to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.

In the aftermath, social media users and influencers have criticized TikTok for hosting the live stream. Instagram user Gina Luciano said: “I find it disgusting and disturbing that TikTok allowed that livestream to go on for as long as it did. It just goes to show you that that app promotes bullying.”

Luciano continued: “Don’t watch that video, don’t watch any clippings of that live stream. It’s not content. It’s not entertainment. It’s a cry for help.”

Dana Bowling, another Instagram user said: “Can we file a class action suit against TikTok for exposing adults and teens to that trauma…? No one should be ok with this.”

Although several users claimed the live stream lasted more than 30 minutes, a TikTok US spokesperson disputed those reports, saying the broadcast was approximately half that length. The spokesperson said TikTok’s automated moderation systems flagged the live stream within minutes and referred it to the platform’s US moderation team for review.

Several subsequent live streams were removed within 90 seconds and Hilton’s account was ultimately banned, the spokesperson added.

The company said it also alerted local law enforcement officials and that the live stream violated its community guidelines, which prohibit content depicting or promoting suicide or self-harm.

Despite TikTok’s removal of the live stream, screen recordings of the footage have since widely circulated across other platforms including X and Instagram, in turn prompting users to advise others to turn off video autoplays and mute mentions of Hilton.

“Assume every Trending Topic link with his name on it will lead you to the video. Don’t click on the link. The video is everywhere right now. To be extra sure, turn video autoplay off (it’s in Settings) and mute the phrase ‘Perez Hilton,’” one person said on Bluesky.

Another person similarly said: “PLEASE mute ‘Perez Hilton’ (as a term) if images of self harm, a person in crisis… are bad for you. Please.”

Other users have encouraged those struggling with mental health issues to seek support. TV personality and influencer Tefi Pessoa wrote on her Instagram story: “If Perez Hilton’s live triggered you in any way, please call 988. There is help, I promise. I love you.”

The Guardian reached out to X for comment. Meta declined to comment.

Many users also commented directly on Hilton’s Instagram posts to express their concern, with one writing: “A lot of people care and are concerned for you. Please take care of yourself Perez. Please know that you are loved.”

Someone else said: “Perez I hope you are stabilized and doing alright now, that video has us all concerned. Please heal up.”

On Wednesday afternoon, Hilton’s team and family released a statement confirming that Hilton is receiving medical care.

“Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez, and we are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers. We can confirm that Perez is receiving medical care, and our family’s focus right now is on his well-being. We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time,” the statement said.

“If and when we are able to share any updates, we will do so with everyone as soon as we can. Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support,” it added.

Hilton, whose real name is Mario Lavandeira, rose to fame in the early 2000s when he started PerezHilton.com, a celebrity gossip blog with aggressive commentary that many, including celebrities, likened to online bullying.

Born in Miami to Cuban parents, Hilton graduated from New York University before working in a variety of roles, including a brief stint as an actor and later as a publicist, before finding success as a celebrity blogger under a moniker inspired by Paris Hilton.

By 2007, the New York Times reported that Hilton was spending 17 hours daily publishing an average of 30 blogposts every day. At the time, his website was charging $9,000 a week for a single advertisement, and as much as $45,000 for its most expensive ad package, the outlet added.

Speaking to the Guardian in 2014, Hilton described himself as being “sassy without being nasty”.

In his 2021 memoir, the father of three reflected on his earlier work, writing: “I have a ton of regrets, particularly because I now see that I never needed to be so mean or cruel.”

Earlier this year, Hilton revealed that he underwent “emergency surgery” for deep vein thrombosis after doctors discovered the condition following a three-week hospitalization due to sepsis.

Reflecting on the experience, Hilton said God “presented himself to me”, adding: “I’ve been crying but happy tears … because this is just …so crazy. I’ve been reading the Bible, and so much of what is said here I had already been thinking of. It’s just overwhelming in the best, most beautiful way.”

articles.title: Lane Kiffin knows there aren’t excuses at LSU. Now comes the test of making it worth the price of admission
articles.excerpt:
Trey Wallace explains why Lane Kiffin has such lofty expectations put on him for his first year of coaching at LSU.

One of the benefits of bringing Lane Kiffin to LSU as head coach has already paid o...
articles.body_text:
Trey Wallace explains why Lane Kiffin has such lofty expectations put on him for his first year of coaching at LSU.

One of the benefits of bringing Lane Kiffin to LSU as head coach has already paid off from a marketing standpoint, thanks to the circus-like atmosphere that followed him from Ole Miss to Baton Rouge towards the end of last season.

As he ushers in a new era of football with the Tigers, the expectations are following him 320 miles south to the Bayou of Louisiana with fall camp getting underway Wednesday morning in the humid atmosphere that is known to plenty around the south.

Lane Kiffin’s Coaching Saga Feels Like A Taylor Swift Album Rollout, With 'Bad Blood' And 'Illicit Affairs'

And with those expectations built from his time at Ole Miss, along with an expensive coaching staff and roster calling Baton Rouge home, come aspirations from a fan base starving to get back into the actual playoff conversation.

Let's all be honest about the situation that Kiffin has embraced with LSU: Every fan or booster that dons the purple and gold around the country are expecting big things in year one from the Tigers.

In reality, there's nowhere to run or hide from what awaits Lane Kiffin when he runs out of the tunnel on Labor Day weekend inside Tiger Stadium with Dabo Swinney's Clemson Tigers awaiting on the other side of the field.

Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers speaks during a press conference at the LSU Football Practice Facility in Baton Rouge, La., on Feb. 4, 2026. (Gus Stark/LSU/University Images)

This is the start of what could be a very prosperous story for the LSU athletic department, along with those who are craving a championship. Now, don't get me wrong, I'm not implying the Tigers will be in contention for a spot in the CFP when the first week of November rolls around this season.

But, that doesn’t mean the LSU faithful aren’t secretly putting that type of pressure on the head coach who has made plenty of headlines during his short-lived stint in Baton Rouge up to this point.

When fans are paying an steep price to get into the show, they want to be entertained, no matter what year this is for the head coach. Over the years, that part has been missing from the LSU football program, lost in the chaos of Brian Kelly's tenure.

Couple that with Kelly's firing last season, and the madness that ensued during a coaching search that garnered non-stop headlines from those who cover the sport, those who are invested in the Tigers football program are expecting a show every weekend.

Ted Cruz Urges Senate To Stay in Washington Until Protect College Sports Act Passes This Week

Whether that is reasonable is up to those who are involved in the daily grind, either on the field or inside the athletic department. Spending over $40 million on a roster that should be able to win this season brings those types of expectations.

That's just the world we live in right now with college athletics, so there's no running from the spotlight.

The moment Lane Kiffin boarded that private jet sitting on an Oxford, Mississippi, tarmac was the turning point in the eyes of the same fans who were listening to Governor Jeff Landry complain about the buyout LSU was having to pay Brian Kelly to go away.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry Says He'd Let Donald Trump Select Next LSU Coach Before Current AD

Head football coach Lane Kiffin and Athletic Director Verge Ausberry of the LSU Tigers arrive at Baton Rouge Metropolitan Airport in Baton Rouge, La., on Nov. 30, 2025. (University Images via Getty Images)

With this type of marketing plan comes great expectations, even if Lane hasn't been enthralled in the hoopla.

"I don't know if I feel a lot of that, and that's not a non-answer," Kiffin started. "I'm in the building so much, I don't really get out a whole lot so I probably don't feel that as much. But when I do get out, I do feel it. I hear out, like with the season ticket sales and fans excitement for the opener. Somebody talked about ticket prices being really high.

"So, I think that's great. I think it's all part of it. When you hire a coach, that's part of what you hire. You hire the energy that comes around it. That's the business element, and that pays off in fan support, donations, in recruiting and players wanting to come."

But, just because someone is bringing excitement to the program doesn’t mean success is going to follow. Selling tickets obviously doesn’t translate to competing at the level in which LSU fans expect.

"Obviously, the number one thing to do is win, to maintain that excitement," Lane Kiffin explained. "With that comes a lot of expectations to perform and do well. And, the expectations are extremely high here, which is ok. I knew that coming in. That matches how I think. So, I know there's not going to be thoughts of well that was the record here last year, so we should just improve a little bit.

"I get it. But, I also know that as we've been here and seen the success of what's come in recruiting and how nationally how recruit have felts that have been here or in this next class, I know that as good as we are right now, this is just the beginning. And, in the season after we'll have a better roster.

Mississippi head coach Lane Kiffin reacts to a official's call during the second half of an NCAA college football game against Mississippi State, Friday, Nov. 28, 2025, in Starkville, Mississippi. (AP Photo/Rogelio V. Solis)

Kiffin understands that excuses aren’t going to fly, even if some are valid about recruiting during a time when coaches were traveling back and forth from Oxford to Baton Rouge.

In reality, the LSU coach lives for these types of expectations, because he felt the same way at his previous stops. It's just how he's built, whether from an entertainment standpoint or seeing results on the field.

But, here we are. After months of waiting, the time to prove himself in a new town is upon us.

Four weeks from now, LSU fans will pack Tiger Stadium expecting a win over Clemson. While there have been hints of that type of feeling around Baton Rouge in previous years at times, this chapter of the Lane Kiffin story will be dictated on how the Tigers perform on the field this season.

It might not be 'fair', but it's just the reality of college football in 2026. And yes, the return to Ole

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: SpaceX shares slide on the heels of first quarterly report
articles.excerpt:
SpaceX share price has plunged more than 13 percent, a day after the Elon Musk-run company reported its first quarterly earnings as a publicly listed company.

On Wednesday, the stock closed down at $...
articles.body_text:
SpaceX share price has plunged more than 13 percent, a day after the Elon Musk-run company reported its first quarterly earnings as a publicly listed company.

On Wednesday, the stock closed down at $108.10, down 13.6 percent from Tuesday’s close of $125.33.

Investors have been spooked by the increase in the company’s capital expenditure. At $18.37bn, it was a six-fold jump from last year, and much higher than the $13.2bn that analysts had forecast.

The majority of that investment, $15.8bn, is earmarked for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, which includes specialised compute, storage, networking and software systems required to build, train, deploy and operate AI models at scale. SpaceX has said it wants to increase the capacity of its data centres from 1.4GW currently to 2GW by year-end.

Investors across the technology sector are questioning whether the large investments in AI infrastructure will actually yield returns.

“We’ve watched the same scrutiny land on Big Tech this earnings season, where investors have questioned open-ended wallets and started demanding a visible return on them,” said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst at trading platform eToro.

“SpaceX faces that test with an added degree of difficulty because it’s asking shareholders to bankroll data centres in orbit.”

SpaceX has said its computing capacity not only serves its Grok models but is also actively sold, with $14.1bn in cloud-services agreements lined up.

The one area that SpaceX saw some profit was from the “connectivity” business, with revenue jumping 66 percent from a year earlier as the number of subscribers to its Starlink satellite communications service doubled to 12 million, bringing in $1.66bn in operating income.

SpaceX’s share price faces another test on Thursday, when the first tranche of the post-IPO lock-up expires, making up to 911.5 million shares, roughly 20 percent of restricted holdings, eligible for sale.

Melissa Otto, head of Visible Alpha research at S&P Global, told Al Jazeera that the stock is “likely to be volatile” once the lock-up lifts.

SpaceX’s IPO was priced at $135 per share and climbed to $225 within days of its June 12 debut, briefly catapulting Musk as the world’s first trillionaire. The stock has since dropped.

articles.title: 5 Mexican cartel bosses charged in timeshare fraud scheme targeting elderly Americans, DOJ says
articles.excerpt: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Justice Department leaders detailed the efforts of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) to target elderly Americans in a sprawling timeshare fraud sc...
articles.body_text:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Justice Department leaders detailed the efforts of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) to target elderly Americans in a sprawling timeshare fraud scheme.

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), along with the heads of numerous other federal agencies, announced Wednesday indictments of members of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) for drug trafficking, weapons charges and for targeting elderly Americans in sprawling timeshare fraud schemes.

The revelation was part of a wider inter-agency news conference Wednesday announcing a sweeping set of enforcement actions targeting the CJNG in Mexico.

"These sophisticated organizations use violence and fear to maintain control over the importation of deadly narcotics in the United States, including fentanyl, cocaine, meth, and other illegal drugs. Their actions spread violence and death to our communities," Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced during the news conference.

"These cartel members have been charged with a range of crimes, including running drug networks, organizing highly trained hitmen responsible for murders and attempted assassinations, procuring weapons, money laundering and deadly drug manufacturing and distribution. Three of the alleged cartel members were also allegedly committing a sophisticated fraud targeting elderly Americans in an alleged timeshare fraud scheme," Blanche added.

'NARCO-TERRORIST' FAMILY MEMBERS TARGETED IN RUBIO'S LATEST VISA CRACKDOWN

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche appears before a Senate Judiciary Committee confirmation hearing for his nomination to be attorney general at the Dirksen Senate Office Building in Washington, D.C., on July 15, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

As part of the enforcement, the DOJ's criminal division brought federal charges against five senior members of the cartel, including drug trafficking and firearms offenses, Assistant Attorney General Tysen Duva said. Duva also provided further details about the fraud scheme targeting elderly Americans.

"CJNG targeted Americans who are aspiring to own or already own timeshares in Mexico, many of them elderly, and promised them profits for selling or renting them. But first, the victims had to pay taxes and advance fees. Of course, the profits never came. Once someone paid, the fraudsters contacted them again, posing as lawyers or officials who could recover the money for another fee," Duva explained.

"Of course it was fake. The scheme morphed and continued, with the fraudsters even claiming that the victims actually paid a cartel and would be arrested if they did not pay more, which they did. One particular victim, an 83-year-old individual, an American who bought a timeshare many years ago for $179,000, was duped at each level of this phase. He paid advance fees to begin with. He fell for fake real estate websites and title companies. He was victimized again by attorneys who sent their bar information and fake websites, who claimed that they could get his money back. Of course they were impersonators and they could not," Duva continued.

FAKE BOOKING.COM TRAVEL CREDIT SCAM TARGETS TRAVELERS

"Government agencies then contacted him for additional fees, using government letterhead and spoofed government websites. And then again, Mexican law enforcement contacted him and demanded he pay criminal and civil fines because he had apparently paid a cartel. It went on and on. It victimized this man for hundreds of thousands of dollars over eight years," Duva said.

Between 2019 and 2023, FBI Director Kash Patel explained during the news conference, the scheme defrauded over 6,000 Americans to the tune of $400 million.

"These individuals, pursuant to the New York Field Office investigation that began a few years ago, started call centers, down south and across the world. The funds they utilized and they scammed out of these call centers from senior citizens from across America, totaled over $400 million. They duped our seniors using email, telephone, text messages and phishing campaigns into subscribing to a timeshare project that they falsely stood up and falsely delivered promises that our seniors would be able to enjoy their lives and their vacations, only to have that money seized from them and that vacation and their retirements deprived from them," Patel said.

Members of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), led by Nemesio Oseguera, known as "El Mencho," participate in firearms training at an undisclosed location in Michoacan state, Mexico. (Stringer/Reuters)

Patel also announced that the FBI had executed over 30 foreign transfers of custody in 15 countries in July alone.

"I'm here to tell you today, for all these individuals that are on the run right now, you will not be on the run for long. We will hunt you down in every corner of the planet, and we will return you here to face American justice," he said. Patel also said the FBI was working to return stolen funds to the elderly victims, adding "we have seized these funds and we are going to get them back to the senior citizens that were fleeced of their life savings and their retirements. That is the mission of law enforcement."

FBI Director Kash Patel speaks during a press conference in Washington, DC on June 23, 2026. (Ken Cedeno/AFP via Getty Images)

Blanche said the DOJ has been working with a wide swath of other federal agencies on increased enforcement actions which he said have helped reduce fentanyl overdose deaths in the U.S. by 22%. The agencies involved in the enforcement actions included the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the IRS, the State Department, Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the Drug Enforcement Agency.

TRUMP 'DRUG CZAR' WARNS OF DEADLY 'RHINO TRANQUILIZER' KILLING AMERICANS AS CARTEL CRACKDOWN ESCALATES

The DEA's Administrator Terry Cole framed the enforcement as an America First policy during the news conference.

"Since the inception nearly two decades ago, CJNG has grown into one of the world's most dangerous and ruthless foreign terrorist organizations. CJNG was built on a vast criminal network that produces and distributes deadly drugs, while sustaining a powerful influence via violence and corruption in Mexico. This includes members within the Mexican government who shield CJNG leadership from justice and facilitate drug trafficking, money laundering, and violence," Cole said.

"CJNG actions have resulted in the deaths of thousands of Americans, Americans that were lost way too soon. They did this through the production and distribution of fentanyl, a weapon of mass destruction. DEA is aggressively targeting both the cartels and the corrupt government officials who are responsible for the deaths of our citizens," Cole continued.

Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, a top figure in the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) known as "El R-1," was taken into custody following a joint military and law enforcement operation. (SSPC - Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana)

"Today's coordinated actions against CJNG leadership and infrastructure, including superseding indictments and rewards totaling more than $100 million in arrest, will not end. It sends a very clear message. This is just the beginning. This is about Americans first. This is a fight against CJNG that we are just beginning, and we will not back down. DEA investigations of cases have generated more than 100 federal indictments against CJNG leaders and members and associates. We are working with our international partners to arrest, extradite, and prosecute these defendants in the United States," Cole concluded.

Blanche said the agency partnered with the State Department to offer up to $100 million for information leading to the arrest of the cartel leaders.

Fox News Digital contacted the DOJ, FBI and DEA for further comment.
